The little girl was thrilled to have the special line. She carried it all around the garden, through the tall grass and around the big tree. Everywhere she went, she carried the green line.

Finally, the little girl got tired. She carefully put the line back down and sat there, admiring it. She would never forget her beautiful green line.

Once upon a time there was a bunny who loved to hop. He hopped around the earth all day long, from one place to the next. His hopping was so popular that everyone wanted to join in!

Soon all the animals in the world were hopping with the bunny. They hopped through jungles and fields, over mountains and rivers. Everywhere they went they found something new and exciting.

At the end of the day, they hopped over to a big field of flowers and laid down in the sun. There they had a nap and laughed and talked until the sky turned dark.

Then, with the stars twinkling above, the bunny and his friends hopped home to their families. They waved goodbye to each other, knowing they'd see each other again soon, and the bunny wished them goodnight.

At the vet's office, the vet looked at the pup's foot and said, "I can take the spike out, but it might hurt a bit." Thankfully it didn't and the pup gave Jim a big lick to say thank you!

The ladybug was very sad about the bad experience. He wanted to be helpful, but he had been warned against touching the poison. He sadly crawled back to his meadow, never daring to peek around another corner again.

Jimbo was so curious. He looked inside the pot and discovered that there were mice swimming in the old soup! He started to laugh with joy.

Once upon a time there was a big train. The engine was old and it needed some help to keep going. So the train driver stopped at a station and bought some new coal. The coal was black and shone like a star. He took the coal and put it in the engine.

The train driver climbed in the driver's seat and waved his flag. The engine started to move. Chugga-chugga-chugga, the engine went as the train filled with smoke. All the passengers waved goodbye as the train took off. 

The engine kept chugging away, burning the black coal as it travelled down the tracks. Everyone on the train was happy because it was going to take them to their destination. 

The train chugged and chugged until it reached the station. Everyone cheered when they finally arrived. The driver took the last of the coal out of the engine, thanked it for all its hard work, and then put it back in the coal store. 

The End.

Tom and Lily were playing in the garden. They saw a big red squash growing on a vine. Tom wanted to pick it and eat it.

"Look, Lily, a red squash! Let's take it and make soup!" Tom said.

"No, Tom, we can't do that. The squash is not ours. It belongs to the farmer. He works hard to provide food for us and others. We should not take what is not ours." Lily said.

"But I'm hungry and the squash looks yummy. And the farmer has many squashes. He won't miss one." Tom said.

He reached for the squash, but Lily stopped him. She pointed to the fence, where the farmer was watching them.

"Tom, look, the farmer is there. He sees us. He is not happy. He is coming to talk to us. We should say sorry and go away." Lily said.

Tom looked and saw the farmer. He felt scared and ashamed. He dropped the squash and ran away with Lily. They went back to their house and told their mom what happened.

Their mom was not happy either. She said they did a bad thing and they should learn to respect other people's things. She said they should go back to the farmer and apologize and offer to help him with his work.

Tom and Lily agreed. They felt sorry for what they did. They went back to the farmer and said sorry. The farmer was still angry, but he accepted their apology. He said they could help him pick some squashes and take them to the market. He said he would give them a small squash as a reward.

Tom and Lily thanked the farmer and helped him. They learned a lesson and enjoyed the squash soup. They decided to never take what is not theirs again.

Anna and Ben were twins who liked to do everything together. They shared a room, a bike, and a big box of toys. They always played the same games and helped each other with their homework. They were very happy.

One day, their mom told them that they had to go to a party at their aunt's house. There would be many people, music, and food. Anna and Ben were excited, but also a little scared. They had never been to a big party before.

"Don't worry, you will have fun," their mom said. "But remember, you have to be polite and respectful to everyone, especially to the old people. They are your family and they love you."

Anna and Ben nodded and got ready. They put on their best clothes and shoes. They also took a gift for their aunt, a nice picture they had drawn together.

At the party, Anna and Ben saw many faces they did not know. Some were young, some were old. Some smiled, some frowned. Some talked, some were quiet. Anna and Ben felt shy and held each other's hands.

They saw their aunt and gave her the picture. She hugged them and thanked them. She said they were very sweet and talented. She also said they looked very cute in their clothes.

"Would you like to dance?" she asked them. "There is a band playing some nice songs."

Anna and Ben looked at each other. They liked music, but they had never danced before. They did not know how to move their feet and arms.

They were about to say no, when they saw an old man sitting in a corner. He had white hair, a long beard, and a cane. He was their grandpa, but they had not seen him for a long time. He looked sad and lonely.

Anna and Ben felt sorry for him. They remembered what their mom had said about being polite and respectful to the old people. They decided to do something nice for him.

They let go of each other's hands and walked to the old man. They smiled and said hello. They asked him if he wanted to dance with them.

The old man was surprised and touched. He smiled and said yes. He took their hands and stood up. He said he used to love dancing when he was young. He said he would teach them some steps.

Anna and Ben followed him to the dance floor. They listened to the music and watched his feet. They tried to copy him. They felt clumsy and silly at first, but soon they felt happy and free. They laughed and spun and jumped. They forgot their fear and shyness.

The old man was happy too. He felt young and alive again. He thanked them for their kindness and courage. He said they were very smart and brave.

The other people at the party watched them and clapped. They said they were very cute and fun. They said they had made the party more lively and joyful.

Anna and Ben looked at each other and smiled. They had learned something new and made someone happy. They had also learned to separate and try new things. They realized that they did not have to do everything together to be happy. They could still love each other and be themselves.

They hugged the old man and thanked him for the dance. They said they loved him and hoped to see him again. They also hugged their mom and their aunt and thanked them for the party. They said they had fun and learned a lot.

They went back to their room, their bike, and their big box of toys. They played the same games and helped each other with their homework. They were very happy.

Mommy heard Lila and opened the door. She saw the bird and Lila and Lizzy. She was angry and scared too. She grabbed a broom and waved it at the bird.

"Go away, you nasty bird!" she shouted. "Leave my Lila and her lizard alone!"

The bird was afraid of the broom and the mommy. It flew away and did not come back. Lila and Lizzy were safe. Mommy hugged them and took them inside.

"Lila, you are very brave," she said. "But you should not play outside alone. The bird could have hurt you or Lizzy."

"I'm sorry, mommy," Lila said. "I love Lizzy. He is my friend. I don't want to lose him."

"I know, honey," Mommy said. "But you have to be careful. There are some bad things in the world that can hurt you or your friends. You have to listen to me and do what I say."

"OK, mommy," Lila said. "Can I keep Lizzy?"

"Of course, you can," Mommy said. "But you have to take good care of him. He is a living thing, not a toy. You have to feed him, clean him, and give him water. And you have to ask me before you take him outside."

"I will, mommy," Lila said. "Thank you for saving us. You are the best mommy ever."

"You're welcome, Lila," Mommy said. "You are the best daughter ever. And Lizzy is a very lucky lizard to have you as his friend."

"What is that?" Lily asked.

One day, Tom has a special event at school. His teacher says they will learn about animals. Tom is happy. He loves animals. He wants to see them and touch them.

The farmer is nice. He shows Tom and his friends how to feed the animals. He gives them corn, hay, and carrots. Tom feeds a cow. The cow licks his hand. Tom laughs. He feels the cow's tongue. He signs "thank you" to the farmer.

The owl nodded. "They are, indeed. But they are also very late for you. You need to sleep and rest, so you can grow and learn. The stars and the moon will be here tomorrow, and the next day, and the next. But you will miss them if you are too tired and grumpy."

Lila and Tom realized that the owl was right. They thanked him for his advice and said goodbye. They wrapped themselves in the blanket and ran back to their house. They climbed into their bed and cuddled each other. They felt warm and safe.

Lila and Tom were friends who liked to play music. Lila had a drum and Tom had a guitar. They would bang and strum and make a lot of noise. They did not care about rhythm, they just wanted to have fun.

One day, they saw a poster for a talent show at the park. It said, "Show your skills and shine on stage! Win a prize!" Lila and Tom wanted to win the prize, so they decided to enter the talent show. They thought they were the best musicians in the world.

They went to the park and saw many other kids with different talents. Some could sing, some could dance, some could do magic tricks. Lila and Tom felt nervous, but they did not practice. They thought they did not need to.

When it was their turn, they went on stage and started to play their music. But they did not sound good. They were out of tune, out of sync, and out of control. The other kids laughed at them and booed them. Lila and Tom felt sad and ashamed. They ran off the stage and hid behind a tree.

A kind lady came to them and said, "Don't be sad, kids. You have a lot of energy and passion, but you need to work on your rhythm. Rhythm is the beat that makes music sound nice and smooth. If you practice and listen to each other, you can improve your rhythm and play better music."

Lila and Tom looked at each other and nodded. They thanked the lady and asked her for some tips. She showed them how to tap their feet, clap their hands, and count to four. She also gave them some smelly cheese to eat, because she said it was good for the voice.

Lila and Tom ate the cheese and practiced their rhythm. They found out that playing music with rhythm was more fun and easier than playing without it. They also sounded better and felt happier.

The next day, they went back to the park and asked the talent show organizer if they could play again. He agreed and gave them another chance. They went on stage and played their music with rhythm. The other kids cheered and clapped for them. Lila and Tom felt proud and happy. They won the prize, which was a big cake. They shared it with the kind lady and the other kids. They learned that rhythm is important for music and for friendship.

Tim and his mom went to the park. They saw a pond with many ducks. Tim liked the ducks. He wanted to feed them bread. He asked his mom for some bread.

"Here you go, Tim. But be careful. Don't go too close to the water. And don't throw the bread too hard. The ducks might get scared," his mom said.

Tim nodded. He took a piece of bread and broke it into small bits. He threw them gently to the ducks. The ducks came closer and ate the bread. They quacked happily. Tim smiled.

One duck was different from the others. It had dirt and mud on its feathers. It looked sad. It did not eat the bread. It stayed away from the other ducks. Tim felt sorry for the dirty duck. He wanted to help it.

"Mom, can I wash the dirty duck? It looks unhappy. Maybe it will feel better if it is clean," Tim asked.

His mom looked at the dirty duck. She thought for a moment. Then she said, "Okay, Tim. But you have to be very gentle. And you have to ask the duck first. Maybe it does not want to be washed."

Tim nodded. He took a bottle of water and a cloth from his mom's bag. He walked slowly to the dirty duck. He said, "Hello, duck. I want to wash you. You have a lot of dirt and mud on you. Do you want to be clean?"

The dirty duck looked at Tim. It saw the water and the cloth. It nodded. It quacked softly.

Tim smiled. He poured some water on the cloth. He rubbed the cloth gently on the duck's feathers. He washed away the dirt and the mud. He did not hurt the duck. He was very careful.

The duck felt the water and the cloth. It felt the dirt and the mud go away. It felt its feathers become soft and shiny. It felt happy. It quacked loudly.

Tim finished washing the duck. He threw the cloth in the trash. He said, "There you go, duck. You are clean now. You look beautiful. Do you feel better?"

The duck looked at Tim. It saw his kind face and his bright eyes. It felt grateful. It nodded. It quacked happily. It gave Tim a kiss on the cheek.

Tim laughed. He said, "You are welcome, duck. I am glad you are happy. You are a good duck. I like you."

His mom watched them. She smiled. She said, "Tim, you did a good thing. You helped the duck. You made it happy. You were very gentle and respectful. I am proud of you."

Tim hugged his mom. He said, "Thank you, mom. I love you. And I love the duck."

The duck quacked. It joined the other ducks. They ate the bread. They played in the water. They were happy.

The end.

Lila and Tom were friends who liked to play outside. One day, they decided to visit a big cliff near their house. They wanted to see the birds and the sea.

"Look, Lila, there are so many birds!" Tom said, pointing at the sky. "They are flying and singing. They are happy."

"Yes, Tom, they are. And look, there is the sea!" Lila said, looking down. "It is blue and shiny. It is pretty."

They walked closer to the edge of the cliff, but they did not see the sign that said "Danger". They did not know that the cliff was not safe.

Suddenly, the ground under their feet started to crack. They felt scared and screamed for help. They held each other's hands and hoped someone would hear them.

Luckily, a man who was walking his dog heard their cries. He ran to the cliff and saw them hanging on the edge. He quickly grabbed a rope and threw it to them.

"Hold on, kids, I'm here to help!" he shouted. "Grab the rope and don't let go!"

Lila and Tom did as he said and he pulled them up. They were very grateful and thanked him.

"Thank you, mister, you saved us!" they said.

"You're welcome, kids, but you should be more careful. This cliff is dangerous. You could have fallen and hurt yourself. You should always listen to the signs and stay away from the edge. Do you understand?" he said.

Benny ate some honey while Lily sang a song. They both had fun and were happy they found the island together.

Lastly, he flew very close to the sun and saw the bright colours and warmth. He wanted to stay there forever but his record book was getting full. With a sad heart he flew away and found his way home. He showed his family all the things in his record book and he was very happy.

Billy pushed harder, higher and higher. He could see all the houses and trees in the distance. He wanted someone to play with. Pushing the swing made him feel better. 

Suddenly, he heard a squeak. He stopped and looked around. There, behind the tree, was a little white bunny hopping toward him. It was so cute. Billy smiled and the bunny hopped closer and closer. He held out his hand and the bunny hopped right onto it.

Billy pushed the swing with one hand and held the bunny with the other. He wasn't lonely anymore. He laughed as the swing went higher and higher and the bunny snuggled in his arms. 

Billy knew he would never be lonely again. He had a special friend with him now, the pink swing and the little white bunny.

As she was putting the dishes away, Lily noticed that some of them were wobbling and about to fall. She tried to balance them, but they still kept wobbling. Suddenly, she had an idea. Lily took a towel and put it under the wobbly dishes. This helped balance them and they stopped wobbling.

Lily's mom was so proud of her for being such a helpful and clever girl. From that day on, Lily always made sure to balance the dishes in the dishwasher so they wouldn't wobble. And she became known as the charming little girl who was great at doing the dishes.

Lily's parents told Mr. Grumpy that it was rude to take things that didn't belong to him. But, Mr. Grumpy didn't care and slammed the door in their faces. Lily never got her ornament back and was very sad. The end.

The bird chirped happily and Lily felt a warm feeling inside her heart. She knew that helping others was the best thing to do. And even though the bird's feathers were a little disgusting from being in the snow, Lily didn't mind at all. She was just happy to have made a new friend.

Once upon a time, there was a little mouse named Timmy. He lived in a hole in the ground. One day, Timmy saw a big, mighty elephant walking by. Timmy was amazed by how big the elephant was. 

"Hello, Mr. Elephant," said Timmy. "Why are you so big?"

"I eat lots of food," replied the elephant. "I also march a lot."

Timmy was curious. "What does it mean to march?" he asked.

"It means to walk in a special way," said the elephant. "I use my big feet to make a loud noise on the ground when I march."

Timmy was impressed. "Wow! You are so mighty!" he said. "I wish I could march like you."

The elephant smiled. "Maybe one day you will," he said. "Just keep practicing." And with that, the elephant continued on his way, leaving Timmy to dream of marching like a mighty elephant.

Buzzy didn't know what to do, so he asked his helpful friend, a bird named Tweety, for advice. Tweety said, "You need to bake some bread. It will help your tummy feel better."

Buzzy had never baked before, but he wanted to feel better, so he followed Tweety's advice. He mixed flour, water, and yeast together and put it in the oven to bake. When the bread was ready, Buzzy ate a slice and felt much better.

From that day on, Buzzy learned to eat in moderation and not to eat too much sugar. He also learned that helpful friends like Tweety are always there to give good advice.

Lily and Tom only had three coins each. They did not have enough money to buy four batteries. They felt sad and angry. They wanted the toy car so much. They thought of a plan. They decided to trick the man and take the batteries without paying.

Tom is a boy who likes to deliver papers. He has a bike and a big bag. Every Wednesday, he rides his bike and puts papers in the mailboxes. He likes to see the people and the houses.

One Wednesday, he sees a new house. It is big and ugly. It has no windows and no flowers. It is dark and scary. Tom does not like the house. He does not want to deliver a paper there.

He rides past the house and goes to the next one. But then he hears a voice. It is loud and angry. It says, "Hey, boy! Where is my paper? I want my paper!"

Tom looks back and sees a man. He is big and ugly too. He has no hair and no teeth. He is wearing a dirty coat and holding a stick. He is standing at the door of the ugly house.

Tom is afraid of the man. He does not want to talk to him. He says, "Sorry, sir. I have no paper for you. I do not know you."

The man says, "That is a lie. You have papers in your bag. Give me one. I need to read the news."

Tom says, "No, sir. These papers are for other people. They pay for them. You do not pay. You do not get a paper."

The man says, "That is not fair. I want a paper. Give me one or I will hit you with my stick."

The man says, "What is it? Hurry up. I have no time."

Tom says, "You have to smile. You have to show me your teeth. Then I will give you a paper."

The man says, "What? That is silly. Why do you want me to smile?"

Tom says, "Because I like smiles. Smiles are nice. Smiles make people happy. You look sad and angry. Maybe a smile will make you feel better."

The man says, "Fine. I will smile. But it will not make me feel better. Nothing makes me feel better. Here, look at my teeth."

The man tries to smile. But he has no teeth. He only has gums. He looks funny and ugly. Tom laughs. He says, "That is not a smile. That is a grimace. You need teeth to smile. Here, take this paper. It has a picture of teeth. Maybe you can learn how to smile from it."

Tom gives the man a paper. It is an old paper. It is not from today. It is from last week. It has a picture of a dentist on the front page. The dentist is smiling and showing his teeth. The man does not notice. He takes the paper and says, "Thank you, boy. You are a good boy. Maybe I will see you next Wednesday."

Tom says, "You are welcome, sir. Maybe you will. Goodbye, sir."

Tom rides away. He is happy. He has delivered all his papers. He has also made a joke. He thinks the man is silly and ugly. But he also thinks the man is lonely and sad. He hopes the paper will make him smile. He hopes the man will get some teeth. He hopes the man will get some friends. He hopes the man will get a nicer house. He hopes the man will be happy. He hopes to see him next Wednesday.

Grandma smiled and said, "I'm glad you like it, Timmy. Now, let's see if you can guess what's inside." 

Timmy shook the gift and heard something zip around inside. He guessed, "Is it a toy car?" 

Grandma laughed and said, "No, but you're close. It's actually a toy race track!" 

Timmy was so happy and played with his new toy all day. He loved it so much that he told his grandma, "This is the best gift ever!"

One day, Lily was playing with her stick when she saw a butterfly. She followed the butterfly around and watched it fly from flower to flower. She was happy to learn about the butterfly and how it liked to drink nectar from the flowers. 

From that day on, Lily loved to learn new things and use her stick to draw pictures and explore the world around her.

Tom decided to buy a new cable box. He went to the store and picked out a shiny, new one. But when he got home, he realized it didn't work with his old TV. Tom was very upset and started to suffer even more. 

Tom tried to return the new cable box, but the store wouldn't take it back. Tom felt very frustrated and didn't know what to do. He tried to watch TV without the cable box, but it just wasn't the same. 

In the end, Tom had to go without TV. He felt very sad and missed his favorite shows. He learned that sometimes modern technology can cause problems and make us suffer.

Once upon a time, in a small pond, there lived a helpful otter named Ollie. Ollie loved to help his friends in the pond. One day, Ollie saw his friend, a little fish named Fin, stuck in a net. Fin was scared and needed help.

Ollie swam fast to Fin and said, "Don't worry, Fin! I will help you get out of the net." Ollie used his sharp teeth to cut the net. He cut and cut until there was a big hole for Fin to swim out.

Fin was so happy and said, "Thank you, Ollie! You are a very helpful otter!" Ollie smiled and swam away to help more friends in the pond. All the animals in the pond loved Ollie, the helpful otter. And they all lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a big red car. The car's name was Rosie. Rosie loved to drive fast and honk her horn. One day, Rosie was driving down the road when she saw a little bird. The bird was deaf and couldn't hear Rosie's horn. Rosie didn't want to scare the bird, so she stopped her car.

The bird was very happy to see Rosie. Rosie asked the bird what its name was, but the bird couldn't talk. Rosie thought for a moment and then had an idea. She put her car in reverse and beeped her horn, but this time she did it very softly. The bird could feel the vibrations and it chirped happily.

Rosie was so happy that she could help the little bird. From that day on, whenever Rosie saw the bird, she would put her car in reverse and beep her horn softly. The bird would chirp and Rosie would honk back. They became good friends and had many fun adventures together.

Together, they cleaned up the glass and made a new glass of juice. From that day on, Lily was more careful when she stirred her juice in the glass.

Lily was very scared and didn't know what to do. She tried to run away, but she was still dizzy and fell down again. The dog came closer and closer until it was right in front of her. Sadly, the story doesn't have a happy ending. The dog attacked Lily and she got hurt. From that day on, Lily always made sure to keep her socks safe and never played near that dog again.

But as Tweetie and her friends were looking at the dictionary, a big cat came out of nowhere and chased after them. The birds tried to fly away, but the cat was too fast. The dictionary fell out of Tweetie's beak and got torn apart by the cat's claws.

The cat thought about it and decided to ask the owner. The owner was a nice lady who said, "Of course you can play with the ball!" The cat and the dog played with the ball all day, and they had so much fun.

In the end, the cat was happy that they asked the question. The dog said, "See? It's always good to ask before taking something." The cat agreed and they went home, tired but happy. The moral of the story is that it's always better to ask a question than to take something without asking.

Just then, she remembered a game her mom had taught her. She said to the clothes, "I'm going to count to three - can you help me?" All the clothes jumped and stopped moving, ready to be gathered.

Lily smiled and said, "One, two, three!" And eventually all her red laundry was safe in the basket.

Lily was so proud of herself for being brave and clever, and went off happily to finish her laundry for the day.

The penny was still feeling impatient but he decided to do as the voice said and he waited. Then, a few moments later, a bridge appeared over the hill. Now he could cross to the other side. Her dad comforted her and wiped her hand. He said it was okay, and that they could find another tomato. He said the worm was hungry and did not know better. He said the soil would use the rot to make more food for the plants.

Lila felt better and smiled. She said she was sorry for the tomato and the worm. She said she would look for a good tomato next time. She said she loved the garden and her dad. He said he loved her too. They went inside to wash their hands and have a snack.

Lily felt sorry for the ant. She thought that the ant might be lonely. She thought that the ant might miss its friends and family. She thought that the ant might want to go back to the garden. She decided to let the ant go.

Lily took the jar to the garden. She opened the lid and tipped the jar over. She watched the ant crawl out. She saw that the ant ran to join other ants. She saw that the ants worked together and helped each other. She smiled and said goodbye to the ant.

Lily learned something new. She learned that ants were amazing and smart. She learned that ants liked to live in groups. She learned that ants were not soft, but they were not mean either. She was glad that she examined the ant, but she was also glad that she set it free.

Lily liked to be organized. She had a place for everything in her room. She had a box for her toys, a shelf for her books, and a drawer for her clothes. She always put things back where they belonged after she used them.

When it was time for bed, Lily felt very hungry. Her tummy was making noises. She wondered why she was so hungry. Then she remembered. She forgot to eat her meal. She felt bad. She knew that eating was good for her.

She went to the kitchen and saw her mom. Her mom was surprised to see her. She asked her what was wrong. Lily told her that she forgot to eat her meal. Her mom hugged her and said that it was okay. She said that sometimes people forget things when they are busy. She said that she was proud of Lily for being organized and helpful.

Lily thanked her mom and ate her sandwich and milk. She felt better. She learned that being organized was good, but not forgetting to eat was also important.

Her mom smiled and said, "No, Sara, you can't take a star from the ceiling. They are too far and too bright. They belong to the sky, not to you."

But she did not know that the ceiling was not real. It was a painting that her dad had made for her. When she poked the star, the paint came off and made a hole. The hole was dark and scary. Sara was scared. She dropped the stick and fell off the chair. She cried and cried.

They were about to grab the bike, when their mom came out.

"Lily and Ben, what are you doing?" she asked.

They looked at their mom, and felt ashamed. They knew they were doing something wrong.

"We are sorry, mom," they said. "We wanted to spoil Tom's bike, because he spoiled our car."

Their mom hugged them and said, "I know you are upset, but spoiling Tom's bike is not the answer. That would only make him more mean, and you more unhappy. You should be kind and forgiving, even to those who hurt you. That is the right thing to do."

Lily and Ben nodded. They realized their mom was right. They let go of the bike, and said, "We are sorry, Tom. We hope you will be sorry too, and fix our car."

Tom, who was hiding behind a bush, heard them. He felt sorry too. He came out and said, "I am sorry, Lily and Ben. I spoiled your car because I was jealous. You have such a nice car, and I have only a bike. But that was wrong of me. I will help you fix your car, and maybe we can be friends."

Lily and Ben smiled. They forgave Tom, and thanked him. They all worked together to clean and repair the car. Then they took turns riding it in the park, with their caps on. They had a lot of fun, and learned a lesson. They learned that spoiling things is bad, but being kind and forgiving is good.

Raoul was walking near a stream. He stopped and looked at the water. The stream looked bad. The water was cloudy and wouldn't move. Raoul wanted to help the stream feel better so he started to talk to it. He said, "Hi stream, why are you so bad?"
The stream didn't reply.
Raoul thought for a moment and then said, "Let me help you!" He started to scoop up buckets of water from the stream and poured it onto the ground. He did this again and again until he was out of breath. Finally, he watched as the stream started to move. The water was clearer and the stream looked much happier. Raoul said, "Thank you for letting me help you!"
The stream replied, "Thank you, Raoul! I'm feeling much better now."

As the sun began to set, Lily started to cry. She was scared and didn't know what to do. Suddenly, a kind and compassionate neighbor heard her cries and came to help. But it was too late. Lily had fallen from the tree and hurt herself badly.

Lily's mommy was so sad and wished she could have saved her. From that day on, she always made sure to check the locks on the gates and keep a closer eye on her little girl.

Ben was not so careful. He pressed hard on his crayons and made thick lines on his paper. He did not mind if they broke or got mixed up. He liked to make loud noises and pretend his crayons were cars or rockets.

"Look, Lila, I made a big rocket!" Ben said, holding up his paper. "It goes zoom, zoom, zoom!"

"That's nice, Ben," Lila said, looking at her paper. "I made a pretty flower. It has many colors and petals."

"Can I see?" Ben asked, moving closer to Lila.

"Be careful, Ben," Lila said, holding her paper away from him. "Don't touch my flower. It is delicate. You might ruin it."

"Hello, mule. We have some treats for you. Do you want some?" Ben said.

The mule looked at them with his big ears and snorted. He did not move from his spot.

"Please, mule. We want to be nice to you. We want to pet you and brush you and make you happy." Lily said.

The mule shook his head and stamped his feet. He did not want their treats or their kindness. He liked to be alone and spoil his mood.

Ben and Lily felt sad and hurt. They turned to leave, but then they heard a voice.

"Wait, children. Don't go. Let me talk to him." It was their grandfather, who was elderly and wise. He walked up to the mule and stroked his mane.

"Hello, old friend. Why are you so mean to these little ones? They only want to show you some love. Don't you remember how we used to play and work together? How we used to have fun and enjoy the sun? Don't you miss that?"

The mule looked at his old master and sighed. He remembered the good times they had, but he also felt old and tired and sore. He did not think anyone cared for him anymore.

"I'm sorry, sir. I'm just a stubborn old mule. I don't mean to be rude, but I don't like change. I don't like new people or new things. I like to be left alone and spoil my day." The mule said.

The grandfather smiled and hugged the mule. He understood how he felt, but he also wanted him to be happy.

Sara and Ben were playing in the park. They liked to run and jump and slide. They saw a big hill with a lot of flowers. They wanted to climb the hill and see what was on the other side.

They ran up the hill, but it was very steep and slippery. Sara fell down and hurt her knee. She cried and said, "Ow, ow, ow! Ben, help me!"

Ben ran back to Sara and hugged her. He said, "Don't cry, Sara. I'm here. Let me see your knee." He looked at her knee and saw a small cut. He said, "It's not bad, Sara. Just a little boo-boo. I have a band-aid in my pocket. I'll put it on your knee and it will feel better."

He took out a band-aid and stuck it on Sara's knee. Sara smiled and said, "Thank you, Ben. You're a good brother. Can we still go to the other side of the hill?"

Ben said, "Sure, Sara. But let's be careful. Hold my hand and we'll go slowly."

They held hands and walked up the hill. When they reached the top, they saw a big surprise. There was a small house with a red roof and a blue door. There was a sign that said, "Welcome to the fairy house. Ring the bell and make a wish."

Sara and Ben were curious and excited. They ran to the door and rang the bell. The bell made a loud and pretty sound. Ding, dong, ding, dong!

Suddenly, a fairy appeared. She had wings and a dress and a wand. She smiled and said, "Hello, Sara and Ben. I'm the fairy of the hill. You rang my bell and made a wish. What do you wish for?"

Sara and Ben looked at each other and thought. They had many things they wanted, like toys and candy and books. But they also remembered how they helped each other and how happy they were together. They said, "We wish for nothing, fairy. We have everything we need. We have each other and we have fun."

The fairy was surprised and pleased. She said, "That's a very wise and kind wish, Sara and Ben. You are good children. You don't need my magic to make you happy. You have your own magic in your hearts. But I'll give you a gift anyway. A gift of joy and laughter. Watch this!"

She waved her wand and made a lot of bubbles appear. The bubbles were big and colorful and shiny. They floated in the air and popped when they touched something. Sara and Ben laughed and clapped and chased the bubbles. They felt dizzy and happy.

The fairy said, "Have fun, Sara and Ben. And remember, the best things in life are not things. They are love and friendship and fun. Goodbye!" She disappeared with a flash of light.

Sara and Ben said, "Goodbye, fairy. Thank you for the bubbles. And thank you for the lesson. We'll always remember it." They hugged each other and went down the hill. They went back to the park and played some more. They were happy and grateful. They had a wonderful day.

Lily and Ben were friends who liked to play in the garden. They had a spray bottle each and they watered the flowers and the grass. They also liked to spray each other and laugh.

One day, they saw a new patch of flowers in the garden. They were very pretty and colorful. Lily and Ben wanted to water them, but they saw a sign that said "Do not spray". They wondered why.

They asked their mom, who told them that the new flowers were very special and delicate. They needed very little water and too much spray would make them sick. She said they could look at them, but not touch them.

Lily and Ben nodded, but they were curious. They wanted to see how the flowers would react to the spray. They waited until their mom was busy and they sneaked to the patch. They each took their spray bottle and sprayed a little bit on the flowers.

The flowers did not like it. They started to wilt and droop. Some of them turned brown and fell off. Lily and Ben were scared. They had ruined the flowers. They ran away and hid.

Their mom noticed the patch and saw what had happened. She was very sad and angry. She looked for Lily and Ben and found them in their room. She asked them why they had sprayed the flowers. They said they were sorry, but they were jealous. They wanted to play with the new flowers too.

Their mom said that being jealous was not a good reason to hurt something. She said that the flowers were a gift from their grandma, who loved them very much. She said that they had to learn to respect and appreciate what they had, and not to ruin what they did not have. She said that they had to help her fix the patch and apologize to their grandma.

Lily and Ben felt very bad. They hugged their mom and said they were sorry. They promised to never spray the flowers again. They helped their mom replant the patch and water it gently. They also made a card for their grandma and said they loved her and her flowers.

The end.

It was a huge field of unknown flowers. She hopped around the field, admiring their unique colors and shapes.

Finally, tired from all of her hopping, she returned to the pond and told the other ducks all about her adventure. She knew that she would never forget the unknown flowers and the joy of hopping.

Once upon a time there was a toy truck. The truck was very special because it had a weight inside it which made it slide very fast. One day the toy truck went out of the house and it rolled down the hill. It went faster, and faster and soon it was too far away to see.

The truck kept going, but eventually the weight came out. The weight was now lost and the truck couldn't slide anymore. 

The little boy was sad. He liked his toy truck and wanted it to be just as it was before. Then he had an idea. He remembered that he had an old toy block with a weight inside, so he decided to put it into the truck. 

The boy started to slide the truck down the hill again and it was going just as fast as before. The truck was even happier than before and the boy was relieved that his toy truck was back to its original condition.

The little girl was so scared that she screamed, "Help! I'm trapped!" But nobody could hear her. She was stuck in the garden and unable to get out.

The little girl cried and cried until she was too tired to cry anymore. Eventually, she made peace with her situation and decided to make the best of the garden. But the little girl never found a way to get out of the garden and she always felt sad when she stepped through the gate.

Anna and Ben say, "Okay, mom, we will be careful. We will come back soon."

But they are not smart and clever. They are silly and foolish. They are cold and sick. They sneeze and cough and shiver. They do not have fun.

They go back inside. They take off their hats and coats. They show their shirts and shorts and sandals. They say, "Mom, we are sorry. We were wrong. We should have listened to you. We should have worn hats and coats. We should not have worn shirts and shorts and sandals. We are cold and sick. We need hugs and kisses and soup."

The end.

But then, they had a problem. They both wanted the same sock. It was a blue sock with a red star. Lily said, "This is my sock. I saw it first." Ben said, "No, this is my sock. I like it more." They pulled and tugged on the sock. They were very frustrated.

"Stop it, you two!" their mom said. She came into the room and saw the mess. "You are making a big noise and a big mess. You need to share the socks. Why don't you part the sock and each take half?"

Lily and Ben looked at their mom. They looked at the sock. They did not want to part the sock. They liked the whole sock. They said, "No, mom. We don't want to part the sock. We want to keep the sock."

Their mom sighed. She said, "Well, then you need to find a way to play with the sock together. Maybe you can take turns, or make a new story, or trade for another sock. But you can't fight over the sock. That is not nice."

Lily and Ben thought for a moment. They did not want to fight. They wanted to play. They said, "OK, mom. We will try to play with the sock together. Thank you for helping us."

Their mom smiled. She said, "You're welcome. I'm glad you are being good twins. Now, let me see your sock show. I'm sure it will be very funny and creative."

Lily and Ben nodded. They put the sock on their hands again. They made a new story with the sock. They made their mom and dad laugh. They were happy.

Anna and Ben swim back to the shore. They dry off with their towels. They are hungry and thirsty. Mom and Dad have a picnic for them. They eat sandwiches and fruit and drink juice. They say thank you and hug Mom and Dad.

Anna and Ben are happy. They had a good day at the lake. They say goodbye to the fish and ducks and frogs. They get in the car and go home. They fall asleep and dream of the lake.

Tom and Lily were twins who liked to play in the garden. One day, they found a bunch of bananas on the kitchen table. They decided to take some and eat them outside.

"Bananas are yummy!" Tom said, peeling one and taking a big bite.

"Yes, they are!" Lily agreed, doing the same.

They ate and ate until they were full. Then they looked at the peels. They were brown and sticky and smelled bad.

"What do we do with these?" Lily asked.

"Let's bury them!" Tom suggested. "Then no one will see them or smell them."

They dug a hole in the garden and threw the peels inside. Then they covered them with dirt and grass.

"There, all done!" Tom said, smiling.

They ran back to the house, feeling proud of themselves.

But the next day, they saw something strange. The hole they had dug was open again. And there were ants and flies and worms crawling all over the peels. And the garden smelled worse than before.

"Uh-oh!" Lily said, feeling scared.

"What happened?" Tom asked, feeling confused.

They heard their mom coming out of the house. She looked angry and sad.

"Tom, Lily, what did you do?" she asked, pointing at the mess.

They hung their heads and told her the truth. They had taken the bananas and buried the peels.

"That was very naughty and wasteful of you!" mom said. "You should have asked me before taking the bananas. And you should have thrown the peels in the compost bin, not in the garden. The peels are good for the plants, but only if they are mixed with other things. If you bury them alone, they attract pests and make the soil unhealthy."

She made them clean up the hole and the peels. Then she gave them a hug and said, "I hope you learned your lesson. Next time, be more careful and respectful of the food and the garden."

Tom and Lily felt sorry and ashamed. They said they were sorry and thanked mom for teaching them. They promised to never do it again.

They learned that burying banana peels was a bad idea. And that being honest and responsible was a good idea. And that mom loved them anyway.

Tom and Sam are friends. They like to play baseball in the park. They have a bat, a ball and a glove. They take turns to hit and catch.

One day, they see a new boy in the park. He has a different bat, a different ball and a different glove. He is bigger than Tom and Sam. He says, "Can I play with you?"

Tom and Sam are not sure. They look at each other. They say, "OK, you can play with us. But you have to follow our rules."

The new boy nods. He says, "What are your rules?"

Tom says, "We hit the ball and run to the tree. Then we run back to the bat. That is one point. We play until we have five points. Then we switch."

Sam says, "We catch the ball with our glove. If we catch it, the hitter gets no point. If we miss it, the hitter gets one point. We try to catch every ball."

The new boy says, "That sounds easy. I can do that. Let me hit first."

Tom and Sam agree. They give him the bat and the ball. They go to the tree with their glove.

The new boy swings the bat hard. He hits the ball far. It flies over the tree and lands on the road. A car honks and stops. The driver gets out and picks up the ball. He looks angry.

Tom and Sam are scared. They run to the new boy. They say, "That was not good. You broke our rule. You hit the ball too far. Now we have no ball. The car man is mad. He might take our ball. What will we do?"

The new boy shrugs. He says, "I don't know. I just hit the ball. That is what you do in baseball. I have another ball in my bag. Do you want to play with that one?"

Tom and Sam shake their heads. They say, "No, thank you. We don't want to play with you. You are different. You don't play nice. You don't listen. You don't care. You are not our friend. Go away."

The new boy frowns. He says, "Fine. I don't need you. I have my own bat, my own ball and my own glove. I can play by myself. You are boring. You are silly. You are not fun. Goodbye."

He takes his bag and walks away. He leaves Tom and Sam alone in the park. They look at each other. They are sad. They miss their ball. They wonder what will happen next.

They looked for a pan to put the mix in. They saw a shiny metal pan on the stove. They did not know it was hot. They reached for it with their hands. They touched the pan and felt a bad pain. They screamed and dropped the pan. The mix spilled all over the floor. They cried and ran to Mom.

One day, Sam saw a new seal at the zoo. He was smaller than the others and had a red ball on his nose. He was very cute and Sam liked him a lot. He asked his mom what his name was. She read the sign and said, "His name is Bobo. He is a famous seal. He was in a movie and a TV show."

Sam was amazed. He wanted to see Bobo do tricks. He waited for the show to start. But when the show started, Bobo did not do anything. He just sat on a rock and looked bored. He did not clap his flippers or make noises. He did not jump or spin or catch fish. He did not even play with his ball. He just quit.

Sam was sad and confused. He wondered why Bobo quit. He asked his mom. She said, "Maybe Bobo is tired of doing tricks. Maybe he wants to have fun with the other seals. Maybe he misses his home in the ocean. Maybe he is not happy here."

Sam felt sorry for Bobo. He wished he could help him. He had an idea. He ran to the gift shop and bought a toy fish. He came back to the seal pool and threw the toy fish to Bobo. Sam was happy too. He smiled and waved at Bobo. He felt like he made a new friend. He decided that Bobo was still a famous seal, but now he was also a happy seal.

Sara and Ben are fish who live in the reef. The reef is their home. They like to swim and play with other fish. One day, they see a big boat on the water. The boat makes a loud noise and drops something in the reef.

"What is that?" Sara asks.

"I don't know. Let's follow it and see," Ben says.

They follow the thing that the boat dropped. It is a big net. The net has many holes. The net catches many fish. Some fish are their friends. The fish are scared and sad. They cannot swim out of the net.

"Help! Help!" the fish cry.

"Oh no! The net is bad. The net hurts the fish. We have to help them," Sara says.

"How can we help them? The net is too big and strong," Ben says.

They look around and see a big rock. The rock has a sharp edge. They have an idea.

"Look! The rock can cut the net. We can push the rock to the net and make a hole. Then the fish can swim out," Sara says.

"Good idea! Let's do it," Ben says.

They swim to the rock and push it hard. The rock moves slowly. They push it harder. The rock moves faster. They push it to the net and the rock cuts the net. The net has a big hole. The fish swim out of the net. They are happy and thankful.

"Thank you, Sara and Ben! You saved us. You are very brave and smart," the fish say.

"You're welcome. We are glad you are safe. The net is bad. The boat is bad. They hurt the reef and the fish. The reef is our home. We have to protect it," Sara and Ben say.

"Look, this is a scale. It can make us shrink or grow," Tom said, putting the scale on the floor.

"Really? How?" Lily asked, not sure what Tom meant.

"Can I do it?" she asked.

Tim and Sam were brothers who liked to play with toys. One day, they saw a vendor selling balloons near the park. The vendor had many balloons of different colors and shapes. Tim and Sam wanted to buy some balloons, but they had no money.

"Can we have some balloons, please?" Tim asked the vendor.

"Sorry, kids, but you need to pay for them. They are two coins each," the vendor said.

Tim and Sam felt sad. They looked around and saw a big tree with many branches. They had an idea.

"Let's attach some balloons to the tree and take them when the vendor is not looking," Sam whispered to Tim.

Tim nodded. They waited until the vendor was busy with other customers. Then they ran to the tree and grabbed some balloons. They tied the balloons to the branches with strings. They thought they were very clever.

They ran back to the vendor and pretended to look at the balloons. They waited for the right moment to take the balloons from the tree.

But they did not notice that the wind was blowing hard. The wind made the balloons shake and pull on the strings. The strings broke and the balloons flew away. Tim and Sam watched in horror as their balloons disappeared in the sky.

"Hey, what are you doing?" the vendor shouted. He saw the broken strings on the tree and realized what the boys had done. He was very angry.

He ran after Tim and Sam and caught them. He scolded them for stealing his balloons. He told them to go home and tell their parents what they had done. He also took away their favorite toys as punishment.

Sara shakes her head and says, "No, this is my car. You have your plane. Go play with your plane."

Ben feels sad and angry. He thinks Sara is not nice. He waits until Sara is not looking and he grabs her car. He runs away with it to his room.

Ben feels sorry and ashamed. He says, "I'm sorry, Sara. I was envious of your car. It is so pretty and shiny. I wanted to play with it. Please forgive me."

Sara looks at Ben and she sees that he is sincere. She remembers that he is her brother and she loves him. She says, "It's okay, Ben. I forgive you. But you have to ask me first before you touch my things. And I have to ask you too. We have to share and be nice to each other."

Ben nods and says, "You are right, Sara. I'm sorry. Can we still play together?"

Sara smiles and says, "Yes, we can. But let's play with both our toys. You can play with my car and I can play with your plane. We can have more fun that way."

Ben agrees and says, "That sounds good, Sara. Thank you. You are a good sister."

Anna and Ben were twins who loved to play on the beach. They liked to build sand castles, collect shells and splash in the water. One day, they saw a big boat on the sea. It was white and shiny and had a flag on it.

"Wow, look at that boat!" Anna said. "I want to go on it and see what's inside."

"Me too!" Ben said. "Let's try to swim to it."

They ran to the water and started to swim. The water was clear and blue, but also deep and cold. They swam and swam, but the boat seemed very far away. They got tired and scared.

"Anna, I can't swim anymore!" Ben said. "I want to go back to the beach!"

"Me too, Ben!" Anna said. "But I don't know which way to go! The boat is blocking the sun and I can't see the shore!"

They started to cry and shout for help. They wished they had listened to their mom, who told them to stay close to the beach and not to go too far into the sea.

Luckily, a man on the boat saw them and heard them. He threw them a rope and pulled them up. He gave them blankets and water and asked them their names and where they came from.

"Thank you for saving us, mister!" Anna said. "We were trying to swim to your boat, but we got lost and scared."

"That was very foolish of you, kids!" the man said. "The sea can be dangerous and you should never swim without an adult. You could have drowned or been hurt by a shark or a jellyfish. You should always be careful and obey your mom."

"We're sorry, mister!" Ben said. "We learned our lesson. We won't swim too far again."

The man smiled and nodded. He called their mom on his phone and told her where they were. He drove his boat back to the beach and gave them back to their mom. She hugged them and thanked the man. She was very angry and relieved.

"Anna, Ben, you scared me so much!" she said. "Don't ever do that again! The sea is not a toy. You have to respect it and be safe."

"We're sorry, mom!" Anna and Ben said. "We love you and we love the sea, but we won't try to swim to a boat again. We promise."

They kissed their mom and went back to their sand castles. They played happily and watched the boat sail away. They knew they had been lucky and they had learned a valuable lesson. They never forgot the man who saved them and the day they tried to swim to the sea.

Bob and Sue played all day long. They skipped on the lawn, chased each other, and laughed a lot. When the sun went down, they said goodbye and went to their homes. They both knew they would play together again soon.

One day, a little boy named Tim went for a walk. He found a long path in the woods. The path was fun to walk on. Tim saw a big tree and heard a loud bird. The bird was singing a happy song.

As Tim walked, he saw a little cat. The cat was wet and dirty. Tim wanted to help the cat. He took a soft cloth and started to wipe the cat. The cat purred and felt better.

Tim and the cat walked back home. They were very happy. They played together all day. Now, Tim and the cat are best friends. They always walk on the path and listen to the loud bird together.

They played with the rock all day, taking turns carrying it in the sack. When it was time to go home, Lily and Ben said goodbye. Lily took her rock home in the sack, excited to show her mom and dad. And from that day on, the gentle girl and her big rock were always together, making her very happy.

Lily put the bean in an envelope and went with her mom to the mailbox. They put the envelope in the mailbox and waited for the mailman to take it away.

A few weeks later, Lily's grandma called to say thank you. She had planted the bean in her garden, and it had grown into a big, beautiful plant. Lily was so happy that she could help her grandma. The moral of the story is that even small things, like a bean, can bring happiness to others when we share them.

Her mom didn't mean to be rude and apologized. Lily forgave her and they finished carving the pumpkin together. They put a candle inside and it looked so pretty. But later that night, Lily forgot to blow out the candle before going to bed. In the morning, the pumpkin was all burnt up. Lily felt sad, but her mom said it was okay and they could get a new pumpkin next year.

Spike was sad and didn't know what to do. He thought and thought until he came up with an idea. He would make a fence around himself with his prickly leaves so the rabbit couldn't eat them anymore. Spike worked hard and made a big fence. The rabbit tried to eat the leaves again, but he couldn't because of the fence.

The rabbit was angry and started to be rude to Spike. He said mean things and tried to knock down the fence. Spike felt scared and didn't know what to do. But then, he remembered that he had made the fence strong and that he could protect himself. So, he stood tall and said, "No! You can't be rude to me anymore." The rabbit realized he was wrong and said sorry. From then on, they became friends and the rabbit never ate Spike's leaves again.

Lily and Ben nodded, but they did not listen. They kept playing with their toys and making more mess. They thought their mom would forget.

But their mom did not forget. She came back after an hour and saw the mess. She was very angry. She said, "Lily and Ben, you did not organize your toys. You did not do what I asked. Now I will take them away and put them upstairs. You will not see them for a long time. Come with me."

Lily and Ben followed their mom upstairs. They were sad and scared. They did not want to lose their toys. They hoped their mom would change her mind.

But their mom did not change her mind. She opened a door and showed them a room. The room was full of toys. Toys of different colors and shapes. Toys that Lily and Ben had never seen before. Toys that looked very fun and impressive.

Lily and Ben gasped. They wanted to play with those toys. They asked their mom, "Mom, whose toys are these? Can we play with them?"

Their mom smiled and said, "These are your toys. These are the toys that you did not organize before. These are the toys that I took away and put upstairs. You did not see them for a long time. Do you remember?"

Lily and Ben remembered. They felt ashamed and sorry. They said, "Mom, we are sorry. We did not organize our toys. We did not do what you asked. Can we have our toys back? Can we play with them?"

Their mom said, "Yes, you can have your toys back. But only if you promise to organize them every day. And only if you share them with each other. Do you promise?"

Lily and Ben promised. They hugged their mom and thanked her. They took their toys and went downstairs. They played with them and organized them. They shared them with each other. They were happy and proud. Their mom was happy and proud too.

Tom was a little boy who liked to wander. He liked to see new things and find new places. One day, he wandered away from his home and into a big field. He saw many green plants with small flowers. He wondered what they were.

He walked into the field and pulled out one of the plants. He saw a brown thing under the ground. It was a potato! He had never seen a potato before. He thought it looked funny and round. He wanted to take it home and show his mom.

He put the potato in his pocket and wandered some more. He saw a wide river with clear water. He liked the sound of the water and the fish that swam in it. He wanted to touch the water and the fish. He walked to the edge of the river and leaned over.

But he leaned too far and fell into the water. He was scared and wet. He cried for help. He felt something pull him out of the water. It was his mom! She had followed him and found him. She hugged him and told him he was safe.

She also saw the potato in his pocket. She smiled and said it was a good find. She said they could cook it and eat it for dinner. Tom was happy and hungry. He learned that wandering was fun, but he should not wander too far or too close to the water. He also learned that potatoes were good to eat. He liked potatoes.

Anna and Ben were going to the airport with Mom and Dad. They were very happy because they were going to fly in a big plane to see Grandma and Grandpa. They packed their bags with clothes, toys and books. They also brought their swimsuits because Grandma and Grandpa had a pool.

At the airport, they saw many people and many planes. Some planes were white, some were blue, some were red. They were very colorful. Anna and Ben liked to watch the planes take off and land. They made loud noises and left white trails in the sky. Mom and Dad checked in their bags and got their tickets. They told Anna and Ben to stay close and follow them.

They walked to the gate where their plane was waiting. They had to go through a metal detector and show their tickets to a lady. She smiled and gave them stickers. Anna and Ben put the stickers on their shirts. They felt like pilots. They boarded the plane and found their seats. They buckled their seatbelts and listened to the instructions. They looked out the window and saw the wing of the plane.

The plane started to move and then went faster and faster. Anna and Ben felt excited and nervous. They held Mom and Dad's hands. The plane lifted off the ground and flew into the air. They saw the airport get smaller and smaller. They saw clouds and birds and cars and houses. They saw a big lake that sparkled in the sun. Anna and Ben wanted to splash in the lake. They wondered if Grandma and Grandpa's pool was as big and shiny as the lake.

The plane flew for a long time. Anna and Ben read their books, played with their toys and ate some snacks. They also took a nap. When they woke up, they saw a different lake. It was smaller and darker than the first one. They also saw mountains and trees and fields. They heard the pilot say that they were almost there. They looked for Grandma and Grandpa's house. They saw a small airport. They saw their plane land and stop. They clapped and cheered. They unbuckled their seatbelts and got their bags. They walked out of the plane and into the airport. They saw Grandma and Grandpa waiting for them. They ran and hugged them. They were very happy. They were ready to splash in the pool.

Lily loves stories. She likes to hear stories from her mom and dad, and she likes to look at stories in books. She has many books with stories, but her favorite one is rare. It is a big book with many colors and pictures, and it has stories about animals and magic. Lily's mom says it is a special book, and she has to be careful with it.

Lily likes to lift the book and put it on her bed. She likes to open the book and see the stories. Sometimes she can read some words, and sometimes she makes up her own words. She likes to pretend she is in the stories, and she talks to the animals and the magic. She has a lot of fun with the book.

One day, Lily's mom has to go to the store. She tells Lily to stay in her room and play with her toys. She says she will be back soon, and she will read her a story. Lily says okay, and she hugs her mom. She waits for her mom to leave, and then she runs to her closet. She knows where the rare book is. She wants to lift it and look at the stories.

Lily reaches for the book, but it is too high. She tries to jump, but she can't reach it. She looks around and sees a chair. She has an idea. She pushes the chair to the closet, and she climbs on it. She is happy. She can lift the book now. She grabs the book and pulls it down. But the book is too big and heavy. Lily loses her balance and falls off the chair. The book falls on the floor with a loud thud.

Lily is scared and hurt. She cries and calls for her mom. She sees the book on the floor, and she sees a tear on the cover. She feels bad. She broke the rare book. She wonders what her mom will say. She hopes her mom will not be mad. She hopes her mom will still read her a story. She hopes her mom will come back soon.

Tom and Amy like to design things with paper and crayons. They cut and color and glue and make animals and cars and houses. They have a lot of fun together.

One day, they find a big black box in the garage. They wonder what is inside. They decide to design a spaceship with the box. They cut a hole for the window and draw buttons and stars and planets. They are very patient and careful.

They finish their spaceship and want to play inside. They crawl into the box and pretend to fly to the moon. They make noises like rockets and aliens. They are very happy.

But they do not know that the box is full of old clothes that Mom wants to give away. Mom comes to the garage and sees the box. She does not see the hole or the drawings. She thinks the box is ready to go. She picks up the box and puts it in the car. She drives away.

Tom and Amy are scared. They shout and bang on the box, but Mom does not hear them. They cry and hug each other. They do not know where they are going. They wish they had not designed a spaceship. They wish they had stayed with their paper and crayons. They are very sad.

One day, Ben and Lily went to the beach with their mom and dad. They brought a big bag with snacks, drinks, toys and towels. Ben and Lily loved to play in the sand and splash in the water. They had a lot of fun.

But then, Ben saw a big wave coming. He wanted to ride it with his floaty. He did not listen to his mom, who told him to stay close to the shore. He ran into the water and jumped on his floaty. The wave was too strong and it flipped him over. He lost his floaty and his towel. He was scared and wet.

Lily saw what happened and ran to help him. She grabbed his hand and pulled him out of the water. She wrapped him in her towel and hugged him. She said, "Are you okay, Ben? You should not go too far in the water. It is dangerous. Mom and dad always explain that to us."

Ben was sorry and ashamed. He said, "I know, Lily. I was silly and did not listen. Thank you for saving me. You are a good sister. And you are lucky you still have your towel."

Lily smiled and said, "I am not lucky, Ben. I am smart. I always listen to mom and dad. And I always share with you. Here, you can have half of my towel. We can dry together."

Ben and Lily hugged and shared the towel. They learned to be careful in the water and to listen to their parents. They also learned to be kind and generous to each other. They had a happy day at the beach.

Anna likes to wear her brown dress. It is soft and has flowers on it. She wears it when she goes to see her grandma. Grandma is very nice and gives her hugs and cookies.

One day, Anna and grandma go to the park. They see many birds and dogs and flowers. Anna runs and plays and laughs. She is very happy. Grandma sits on a bench and watches her.

After a while, Anna feels tired. She goes back to grandma and sits on her lap. Grandma says, "You are a good girl, Anna. Do you want a massage?" Anna nods and smiles. Grandma rubs her back and her arms and her legs. It feels good and warm. Anna says, "Thank you, grandma. I love you." Grandma says, "I love you too, Anna. You are my sweetie pie." They hug and kiss. Anna feels happy and sleepy. She closes her eyes and rests on grandma's chest. Grandma sings a soft song. They are both happy.

Anna and Ben were playing in the park when it started to rain. They ran to a big tree and hid under its leaves. But the rain was too strong and they got wet.

"Look, there is an umbrella!" Ben said. He pointed to a blue umbrella on a bench. "Let's go get it!"

Anna and Ben ran to the bench and grabbed the umbrella. They opened it and held it over their heads. They felt happy and dry.

But then they heard a voice. "Hey, that's my umbrella!" It was an old lady with a cane. She was walking towards them. She looked angry.

"Sorry, lady, we didn't know!" Anna said. She gave the umbrella back to the lady.

The lady took the umbrella and smiled. "It's okay, kids. I'm not mad. You can share my umbrella with me. I have a boo-boo on my leg and I need to go to the doctor. He will heal it for me."

Anna and Ben felt sorry for the lady. They walked with her to the doctor. They told her stories and jokes. They made her laugh.

"You are very kind and funny, kids," the lady said. "You are not silly at all. You are smart and sweet. Thank you for helping me."

Anna and Ben smiled. They were happy to help the lady. They learned that sharing is good and that healing is not only for boo-boos, but also for hearts.

Lily was a dog who liked to run and play. She had a red collar with a bell that jingled when she moved. She lived with a boy named Tom and his family. They loved Lily very much and gave her food and water and hugs.

One day, Tom and Lily went to the park with a ball. They saw other dogs and children there. Tom threw the ball and Lily ran after it. She was very fast and happy. She caught the ball and brought it back to Tom. He said, "Good girl, Lily! You are so smart and fun!"

They played for a long time, until Lily got tired. She lay down on the grass and closed her eyes. Tom sat next to her and petted her fur. He said, "You are the best dog in the world, Lily. I'm so glad you are mine."

But then, something bad happened. A big dog came running towards them. He had a black collar with spikes and a loud bark. He wanted the ball that Lily had. He jumped on Lily and tried to take it from her mouth. Lily was scared and angry. She growled and bit the big dog's ear. The big dog yelped and let go of the ball. He ran away, but not before he snapped at Lily's collar. He broke the bell and made it fall off.

Lily felt sad and hurt. She looked at her collar and saw the empty spot where the bell used to be. She liked her bell. It made her feel special and ordinary. She whimpered and licked her paw. Tom saw what happened and ran to Lily. He said, "Oh no, Lily! Are you okay? I'm sorry the big dog was mean to you. He was a bad dog. You are a brave dog."

He picked up the bell and put it in his pocket. He hugged Lily and said, "Don't worry, Lily. I will fix your collar. I will find a new bell for you. You will still have your jingle. You will still be my Lily."

Lily wagged her tail and licked Tom's face. She felt better and loved. She knew Tom was right. She was still his Lily. And he was still her Tom. They were friends forever.

Sara and Ben like to play in the river. They have a big raft that they can sit on and float. Sometimes they see fish and frogs and birds. They like to sing songs to them.

One day, they meet a boy on the other side of the river. He has a stick and a stone. He throws the stone at the raft and makes a hole. The raft starts to sink. Sara and Ben are scared and angry.

"Hey, why did you do that?" Ben shouts at the boy.

"Because I don't like you. You are ignorant. You don't know anything," the boy says.

"That's not true. We know many things. We know how to sing and how to make friends. You are ignorant. You don't know how to be nice," Sara says.

The boy does not listen. He laughs and runs away. Sara and Ben swim to the shore. They are wet and sad. They look at their raft. It is broken and useless.

They hug each other and start to sing. They sing a song about hope and love. They sing a song that makes them feel better. They sing a song that the boy will never hear.

Tom and Lily were twins who liked to play outside. They had a big yard with a hill and a tree. One day, it was winter and there was snow everywhere. Tom and Lily put on their coats, hats, boots and gloves and ran outside.

"Let's make a snowman!" Lily said.

"OK!" Tom said. They rolled big balls of snow and stacked them on top of each other. They found a carrot, a hat, a scarf and some rocks to make the snowman's face and clothes.

"Look, our snowman is high!" Tom said. He was proud of their work.

"Yes, he is very high!" Lily said. She smiled and hugged Tom.

They heard a loud bark and saw their dog, Rex, running towards them. Rex was a big, furry dog who liked to play too. He jumped on the snowman and tried to bite the carrot nose.

"Rex, no!" Tom and Lily shouted. They ran to stop him, but it was too late. Rex tore the snowman apart with his paws and teeth. He scattered the snow, the carrot, the hat, the scarf and the rocks all over the yard.

Tom and Lily were sad and angry. They loved their snowman and Rex ruined it.

"Bad dog!" Tom said. He scolded Rex and waved his finger.

"Go away!" Lily said. She cried and threw a snowball at Rex.

Rex did not understand why they were mad. He thought he was playing too. He wagged his tail and licked their faces.

Tom and Lily looked at each other and sighed. They knew Rex did not mean to be bad. He was just a silly dog. They decided to forgive him and play with him instead.

"Maybe we can make another snowman later," Tom said.

"Or a snow fort," Lily said.

They laughed and hugged Rex. They had fun in the winter, even if their snowman was gone.

Tom and Lily were twins who liked to play outside. One day, they saw a big hill near their house. They wanted to climb it and see what was on the other side. They asked their mom if they could go, and she said yes, but be careful.

They put on their boots and coats and ran to the hill. It was very steep and covered with grass and rocks. They held hands and started to climb. They saw birds and flowers and bugs on the way. They were having fun.

But when they reached the top, they saw something they did not like. On the other side of the hill, there was a valley full of trash. There were cans and bottles and bags and wrappers and old shoes and rotten food. It smelled bad and looked disgusting. Tom and Lily felt sick.

They wanted to go back to their house, but they did not know how. The hill was too steep to go down the same way they came up. They looked around and saw a path that went around the hill. They decided to follow it.

But the path was slippery and muddy. As they walked, they slipped and fell many times. They got dirty and wet and hurt. They cried and wished they never climbed the hill. They wished they were home with their mom.

After a long time, they saw their house in the distance. They were happy and ran towards it. But they did not see a big puddle in front of them. They slipped and splashed into the water. They were soaked and cold and sad.

Their mom heard them and came out. She saw them and gasped. She asked them what happened and where they went. They told her about the hill and the valley and the path and the puddle. She hugged them and said they were very brave, but also very silly. She took them inside and gave them a bath and a snack and a kiss. They said they were sorry and they learned their lesson. They never climbed the hill again.

Anna loved to play in the garden with her doll, Lily. She liked to pretend that Lily was a princess and the flowers were her friends. She would make crowns and necklaces out of the petals and sing songs to them.

One day, she saw a new flower in the garden. It was big and red and had many layers. Anna thought it was the most beautiful flower she had ever seen. She ran to it and picked it up to show Lily.

"Look, Lily, look! This is a special flower. It is called a rose. It is for you, my princess," she said.

But as she held the flower, she felt a sharp pain in her finger. She looked and saw a drop of blood. She had pricked herself on a thorn.

"Ow, ow, ow! This flower hurts me! It is a bad flower!" she cried.

She threw the flower on the ground and ran to her mother, who was sitting on a bench nearby. She showed her the wound and sobbed.

"Mommy, mommy, help me! The flower bit me!"

Her mother hugged her and wiped her tears. She took a band-aid from her purse and put it on Anna's finger.

"It's okay, sweetie. The flower didn't mean to hurt you. It has thorns to protect itself from animals and bugs. It is a part of the flower, just like the petals and the stem. The flower is not bad, it is just different. And it is very pretty, don't you think?"

Anna looked at the flower again. She saw that it was still blooming, even though she had picked it. She felt sorry for the flower. She had taken it away from its home and its friends. She had been mean to it.

She nodded at her mother and sniffed.

"Yes, mommy, it is pretty. But it is also poor. Can we put it back in the garden? Maybe it will be happy again."

Her mother smiled and kissed her cheek.

"Of course, we can. That is very kind of you, Anna. Come on, let's go and find a nice spot for the rose."

They walked back to the garden and planted the flower in a sunny place. Anna apologized to the flower and gave it a gentle pat.

"I'm sorry, rose. I hope you like it here. You are a special flower. And you are my friend," she said.

The flower seemed to glow in the sun. Anna felt a warm feeling in her heart. She took Lily's hand and waved to the flower.

"Bye, bye, rose. See you tomorrow."

Anna and Ben were playing in the park. They liked to slide, swing and run. They saw a big pole with a sign on it. The sign said "No dogs allowed".

"Look, a pole!" Ben said. "Let's climb it!"

"No, Ben, we can't," Anna said. "The sign says no dogs. Maybe there is a dog inside the pole. It might bite us."

Ben did not listen to Anna. He was a spoiled boy. He always did what he wanted. He ran to the pole and tried to climb it.

"Ben, stop!" Anna shouted. "You are breaking the rule!"

But Ben did not stop. He climbed higher and higher. He reached the top of the pole. He felt proud and happy. He looked down and saw Anna. He stuck out his tongue at her.

"Ha ha, I did it!" he said. "You are a scaredy-cat!"

Anna felt angry and sad. She did not like Ben. He was mean and rude. She wished he would fall off the pole.

Suddenly, a loud bark came from inside the pole. A big, black dog jumped out of a hole. It was angry and hungry. It saw Ben on the pole. It wanted to bite him.

"Help, help!" Ben screamed. "There is a dog! It is going to get me!"

Anna saw the dog. She was scared for Ben. She forgot that he was mean and rude. She wanted to help him.

"Ben, hold on!" she said. "I will get help!"

She ran to the park keeper. She told him about the dog and the pole. He followed her to the pole. He had a leash and a bone. He called the dog by its name. It was his dog. He had put it inside the pole to keep it safe.

"Rex, come here!" he said. "Good boy, good boy. Here is a bone for you."

The dog heard the park keeper. It left Ben alone. It ran to the park keeper. It took the bone and the leash. It wagged its tail.

The park keeper helped Ben down from the pole. He was shaking and crying. He had a scratch on his arm. He was sorry for breaking the rule.

"I'm sorry, I'm sorry," he said. "I was wrong. I should have listened to Anna. She was right. There was a dog inside the pole. It was scary."

The park keeper looked at Ben. He was not angry. He was glad that he was not hurt.

"It's okay, Ben," he said. "You learned your lesson. Next time, you will follow the sign. And you will be nice to Anna. She is a good friend. She tried to save you."

Ben nodded. He looked at Anna. She was still angry and sad. He felt bad. He wanted to make up with her.

"Anna, I'm sorry," he said. "You are not a scaredy-cat. You are brave and smart. You are a good friend. Can you forgive me?"

Anna looked at Ben. She saw that he was sorry. She felt sorry for him too. He had a scratch on his arm. He was scared by the dog. She decided to forgive him.

"Okay, Ben, I forgive you," she said. "But don't do it again. And don't stick out your tongue at me. It's not nice."

Ben smiled. He hugged Anna. He thanked her for helping him. He said he would be nice to her. He said he would follow the sign.

They became friends again. They played in the park. They slid, swung and ran. They did not climb the pole. They did not bother the dog. They had fun. They were happy.

But Tim is not a good player. He is lazy and selfish. He does not pass the ball to Sam or the other players. He only wants to score by himself. He thinks he is the best.

Sam is angry with Tim. He tells him to play better. He says, "Tim, you are a bad player. You are boring. You make our team lose. You need to share the ball and help us."
