Tim is sad and mad too. He cries and says, "No, coach, please. I want to play. I am sorry. I will play better next time."

But the coach does not change his mind. He says, "No, Tim, you have to learn your lesson. Maybe next time you will be a better player and a better friend."

Sam feels sorry for Tim. He says, "Tim, I am sorry I was angry with you. I know you like to play soccer. But you have to be nice and fair to the other players. They are your friends. They want to have fun and win too."

Tim says, "I know, Sam. I am sorry too. I was not nice and fair to you and the other players. I was boring and selfish. I will try to be a better player and a better friend next time."

Sam says, "That's good, Tim. I hope you can play with us again soon. I like to play soccer with you. But you have to share the ball and help us."

Tim says, "I will, Sam. I will share the ball and help you. Thank you for being my friend."

Sara and Ben are twins. They like to play together. One day, they find a big book in the attic. The book has many pictures of people doing yoga. Yoga is when you bend and stretch your body in different ways.

"Look, Ben, this is yoga!" Sara says, pointing at the book. "Can we try it?"

"Okay, Sara, let's try it. But we need a mat to do yoga on. Where can we find a mat?" Ben says.

They look around the attic and see a big, fluffy rug. It is green and soft. They decide to use it as a mat.

"Ben, can you help me carry the rug?" Sara asks. "It is too heavy for me."

"Sure, Sara, I can help you. Let's carry it together." Ben says. They lift the rug and carry it downstairs to the living room. They spread it on the floor and open the book.

They try to copy the pictures in the book. They bend and stretch their arms and legs. They twist and turn their bodies. They make funny shapes and noises. They have fun doing yoga.

But they do not notice that someone is watching them. It is their cat, Fluffy. Fluffy is curious and mysterious. He likes to hide and spy on Sara and Ben. He thinks they are doing something strange.

He jumps on the rug and joins them. He pounces and scratches the book. He meows and purrs. He tries to do yoga too.

Sara and Ben see Fluffy and laugh. They hug and pet him. They invite him to do yoga with them.

"Fluffy, you are silly. You are not a person, you are a cat. You cannot do yoga like us." Sara says.

"Maybe he can, Sara. Maybe he is a yoga cat. He is very flexible and graceful." Ben says.

They all do yoga together. They are happy and relaxed. They love each other and their mysterious cat.

Tom and Lily were playing in the park. They saw a big, hairy dog. The dog was friendly and wagged its tail. Tom liked the dog and wanted to pet it. He asked Lily, "Can I touch the dog?"

Lily was scared of the dog. She shook her head and said, "No, Tom, the dog is too big and hairy. It might bite you."

Tom did not listen to Lily. He walked towards the dog and reached out his hand. The dog barked and snapped at Tom. Tom screamed and ran back to Lily. He was crying and his hand was bleeding.

Lily hugged Tom and said, "I told you not to touch the dog, Tom. You should have listened to me."

A man came running to them. He was the owner of the dog. He said, "I'm sorry, kids, my dog is not used to strangers. He is very cross today. Are you okay?"

Lily nodded and said, "We are okay, but Tom's hand is hurt. Can you help us?"

The man took out a bandage and wrapped it around Tom's hand. He said, "There, that should stop the bleeding. I'm sorry again, kids. Next time, please ask before you pet a dog. Some dogs are not friendly."

Tom and Lily said, "Thank you, sir. We are sorry, too. We learned our lesson. We will not touch a dog without asking."

The man smiled and said, "You're welcome, kids. Be careful and have fun."

He took his dog and left. Tom and Lily went back to playing in the park. They stayed away from the big, hairy dog.

Lily wanted to wear her red coat today. It was cold and windy outside, and she liked how the coat felt warm and soft. She put on her coat and tried to close the zipper, but it was hard. She pulled and pushed, but the zipper did not move. She started to feel angry and sad.

"Mommy, help me!" she cried. "I can't do it!"

Mommy came and saw Lily struggling with the zipper. She smiled and hugged her.

"It's okay, Lily. Sometimes zippers are tricky. You just need to be patient and careful. Do you want me to show you how?"

Lily nodded. She wanted to learn how to close the zipper by herself.

Mommy took the zipper and said, "Look, Lily. You have to make sure the two sides are lined up. Then you have to slide the zipper up slowly and gently. Like this."

She moved the zipper up a little bit, and then let Lily try. Lily copied what Mommy did, and the zipper went up a little more. She felt happy and proud.

"Good job, Lily! You're doing great. Keep going until the zipper is all the way up."

Lily continued to slide the zipper up, until it reached the top. She clapped her hands and cheered.

"I did it, Mommy! I did it!"

Mommy hugged her again and said, "You did it, Lily! You're so smart and brave. I'm very proud of you."

Lily smiled and said, "Thank you, Mommy. You're very wise and kind. I love you."

"But it might be interesting," Tim said. "Maybe the witch has a magic wand or a broomstick or a cauldron. Maybe she will give us some candy or a toy."

Lily was not sure, but she followed Tim to the door. They knocked softly and waited. No one answered. Tim tried to open the door, but it was locked.

"Maybe we should go back," Lily said.

But before they could turn around, they heard a loud voice from inside the house.

"Who is there? Who dares to disturb me?" the voice said.

Tim and Lily were very afraid. They recognized the voice. It was the witch. She was angry and sounded like she was coming to the door.

"Run!" Tim shouted.

They ran as fast as they could, but the witch was faster. She opened the door and saw them.

"Stop, you little pests!" she yelled. "You will pay for your rudeness. I will turn you into something ugly and small."

She raised her hand and pointed at them. Tim and Lily felt a strange tingling in their bodies. They looked at each other and screamed. They were no longer children. They were snails.

The witch laughed and picked them up. She put them in a jar and closed the lid.

"Now you will remain snails forever," she said. "You will be my pets and do what I say. That will teach you to be nosy and bother me."

She took the jar to her house and put it on a shelf. Tim and Lily looked at each other and cried. They wished they had never gone to the witch's house. They wished they had listened to Lily. They wished they could be children again. But it was too late. They were stuck in the jar, with no hope of escape. They learned a hard lesson. The witch's house was not interesting. It was dangerous.

"It's OK, Ann," he said. "But we have to clean up before Mom comes. She will be here soon. Come on, let's get a cloth and some water."

They got a cloth and some water. They tried to wipe the cake mix off the floor, the table, the wall and themselves. But it was hard. The cake mix was sticky and gooey. They needed more water and more cloth.

They did not hear the door open. They did not see Mom come in. They did not notice her turn and gasp. They only heard her voice.

"What is going on here?" Mom asked. She sounded surprised and angry. She saw the cake mix everywhere. She saw Tom and Ann with the cloth and the water. She saw the bowl and the spoon and the ingredients.

Tom and Ann looked at Mom. They felt scared. They knew they were in trouble. They did not know what to say.

They had tried to make a cake for Mom. But they had been too careless. They had made a big mess instead.

She said, "Lisa and Ben, you did not do what I asked. You did not nap and you did not tidy your room. You were naughty. Now you have to give me your gems. You can have them back tomorrow, if you behave."

Lisa and Ben felt sad and sorry. They realized that they had made a mistake. They said, "We are sorry, mom. We should have listened to you. We should have napped and tidied our room. We love our gems, but we love you more. Please forgive us."

Mom hugged them and said, "I forgive you, Lisa and Ben. I love you too. But you have to learn to follow the rules. They are for your own good. Now, try to nap and have sweet dreams. Tomorrow, you can play with your gems again, if you are good."

Lisa and Ben nodded and said, "Okay, mom. Thank you. We will nap and be good." They closed their eyes and fell asleep. They dreamed of their gems and their mom.

The moral of the story is: Listen to your mom and follow the rules. They are for your own good. And don't be greedy with your toys. Share them and take care of them.

Then, the old planes came out. They were smaller and slower than the jets. They had propellers and wings. They looked like toys. Sara and Ben were not very impressed.

But then, something amazing happened. The old planes started to shoot at each other. They made loud bangs and smoke. They pretended to be in the big war. Sara and Ben gasped. They were scared.

"Dad, why are they shooting at each other? I thought they were friends!" Sara cried.

"Don't worry, Sara. It's just a display. They are not really shooting. They are just showing us how they fought in the big war. It's like a game," Dad said.

"But it's not a fun game, Dad. It's a scary game. I don't like it," Ben said.

"I know, Ben. It's not a fun game. It's a sad game. That's why we don't want to have another big war. We want to have peace and friendship," Dad said.

Sara and Ben hugged their dad. They understood. They hoped the old planes would stop shooting and be friends.

The air show ended. The jets and the old planes landed. Sara and Ben were hungry. Dad took them to a food truck. They bought hot dogs and ice cream. They ate them and smiled. They were delicious. They forgot about the scary display. They were happy.

"Can we go near it?" Ben asked.

Mom and Dad said no. They said the whale was too far and too big. They said the whale might be scared or angry if they went near it. They said the whale needed space and respect.

Lily and Ben were sad. They wanted to see the whale closer. They had an idea. They took their buckets and shovels and started to dig a big hole in the sand. They wanted to fill the hole with water and make a pool for the whale.

They worked hard and dug and dug. They ran to the water and filled their buckets. They poured the water into the hole. They did this many times. They thought the whale would like their pool.

But the water did not stay in the hole. It seeped into the sand and disappeared. The hole was always empty. Lily and Ben were confused and tired.

"Why is the water gone?" Lily asked.

Lily and Ben smiled. They waved at the whale. They learned a lesson. They learned to love and care for the animals, but also to let them be. They learned to fill their hearts with kindness, not their holes with water.

"Yes, he is, sweetie. Do you know what he is doing?" mom asked.

"He is playing!" Tom said.

"That's right, he is playing. But he is also trying to stay cool. Hippos need water to keep their skin wet and soft. If they stay out of the water for too long, their skin can crack and hurt. That's why they dry themselves with mud or sand sometimes." mom explained.

"Oh, I see. That's smart!" Lily said.

They watched the hippo for a while, until he got restless. He wanted to find more water and mud. He got out of the pond and walked around the fence. He saw a big fountain in the middle of the zoo. He thought it looked like a nice place to swim and dry himself.

"Hey, where are you going?" one of his friends called.

"I'm going to the fountain. It looks fun!" the hippo said.

"But that's not for us. That's for the people. They will be mad if you go there." his friend warned.

"I don't care. I'm hot and bored. I want to try something new." the hippo said.

He ignored his friend and ran to the fountain. He jumped in and made a big splash. The water was cold and fresh. He felt happy and free. He opened his mouth and sprayed water in the air. He rolled in the mud and sand that was around the fountain. He dried himself and felt good.

The hippo did not understand. He thought he was just having fun. He did not mean to scare anyone. He just wanted to cool off and dry himself. He felt sad and confused. He wished he had listened to his friend.

The zookeepers and the police came and tried to catch the hippo. They used ropes and nets and trucks. They were careful and gentle. They did not want to hurt the hippo. They just wanted to take him back to his pond.

The hippo saw them and realized he had made a mistake. He felt sorry and ashamed. He did not want to cause any trouble. He wanted to go back to his pond and his friends. He followed the zookeepers and the police. He let them put him in a truck. He hoped they would forgive him.

From that day on, Tweetie flew and surfed with caution, always being alert and asking for help when needed. And Tweetie lived happily ever after. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to go fishing with her grandpa, who always had a big smile on his face. One day, they went to the lake to catch some fish. As they were fishing, Lily felt a tug on her hook. She got excited and pulled the fishing rod, but the fish got away.

Lily's grandpa said, "You need to listen carefully to the sound of the water. When you hear a fish nibbling, you have to be patient and wait for it to bite." Lily nodded her head and tried again. She listened carefully and soon enough, she felt another tug on her hook. This time, she waited patiently and caught a big fish!

As they were packing up, Lily's grandpa said, "Now, we have to be careful and hide our fish in the cooler. Otherwise, the other animals might smell it and come to take it away." Just as they were about to leave, a sneaky raccoon appeared and tried to steal their fish! Lily's grandpa scared the raccoon away and they went home happily with their catch.

"I have a towel," said his friend, a little rabbit named Rosie. "You can use it to dry off." 

Ben took the towel and used it to dry himself off. "Thanks, Rosie," he said. "Now I can settle down and relax." 

The friends sat down on the grass and enjoyed the sunshine. "I love being with my friends," said Ben. "It's always so much fun." 

Rosie smiled. "Me too," she said. "We have the best adventures together."

Once upon a time, there was a mule named Jack who lived on a farm. One day, Jack saw a weird-looking scarecrow in the field. "What's that?" asked Jack. "It's a scarecrow," said the farmer. "It scares the birds away from our crops." 

Later that day, the farmer started a fire to burn some old branches. Jack watched the flames and said, "Fire is hot!" The farmer agreed and warned Jack to stay away from the fire. 

Suddenly, the wind blew the weird scarecrow into the fire! "Oh no!" cried the farmer. "The scarecrow is burning!" Jack brayed loudly and said, "We need to save it!" The farmer grabbed a bucket of water and they put out the fire. 

The scarecrow was all burnt and black, but Jack thought it looked even weirder now. "It's okay," said the farmer. "We can make a new one." And they did. From that day on, Jack made sure to keep an eye on the new scarecrow so it wouldn't burn again.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they find a big bag of peanuts on a bench. They are hungry and want to eat some.

"Can we have some peanuts?" Anna asks Ben.

"I don't know. Maybe they belong to someone else," Ben says.

"Maybe they are a gift from God. He gives us good things to eat," Anna says.

She picks up a peanut and holds it in her hand. She closes her eyes and says, "Thank you, God, for this peanut. Please bless it and make it yummy. Amen."

She opens her eyes and smiles. She cracks the peanut and eats it.

"Mmm, it is yummy. You should try one, Ben," she says.

Ben is not sure. He knows that some people are allergic to peanuts. They can get sick and need a doctor. He does not want to get sick.

"I don't think I want to eat a peanut. Maybe I am allergic," he says.

He puts the bag of peanuts back on the bench. He looks around and sees a man walking towards them. The man has a hat and a coat. He looks angry.

"Hey, you kids! What are you doing with my peanuts?" the man shouts.

He runs to the bench and grabs the bag of peanuts. He glares at Anna and Ben.

"These are my peanuts. I bought them for my lunch. How dare you touch them?" he says.

He opens the bag and takes out a handful of peanuts. He puts them in his mouth and chews.

Suddenly, he coughs and wheezes. His face turns red and swollen. He drops the bag of peanuts and clutches his throat.

"Help! Help! I can't breathe! I'm allergic to peanuts!" he cries.

Anna and Ben are scared. They don't know what to do. They see a woman nearby. She has a badge and a walkie-talkie. She is a park ranger. She is dependable. She can help.

"Miss, miss, please help! That man is sick. He ate some peanuts and he is allergic," Ben says.

The park ranger hears Ben and sees the man. She runs to him and calls for help on her walkie-talkie.

"Don't worry, kids. I'm here to help. I have a medicine that can help him. Stay back and be calm," she says.

She takes out a small device from her pocket. It has a needle and a button. She presses the needle against the man's leg and pushes the button. The device makes a click sound. It injects some medicine into the man's body.

The man stops coughing and wheezing. His face returns to normal. He breathes easier.

"Thank you, thank you. You saved my life. I'm sorry for yelling at you, kids. I didn't know I was allergic to peanuts. I never ate them before," he says.

The park ranger smiles and nods. She checks the man's pulse and blood pressure. She tells him to sit down and rest.

"You're welcome, sir. You're lucky I was nearby. You had a severe allergic reaction. You need to see a doctor and avoid peanuts from now on," she says.

She turns to Anna and Ben and gives them a hug.

"You did a good job, kids. You were brave and smart. You found me and told me what happened. You are good helpers," she says.

Anna and Ben feel happy and proud. They hug the park ranger back.

"Thank you, miss. You are a good helper too. You are dependable. God sent you to help us," Anna says.

The park ranger smiles and says, "You're welcome, Anna. God sent you to help me too. You prayed for the peanut and thanked God for it. You reminded me to be grateful for everything He gives us. You are a good girl."

They all smile and thank God for His help and love. They wait for the ambulance to arrive and take the man to the hospital. They hope he will be okay. One day, Tim and Sam were playing in their room. Tim had a big truck that could lift things with a hook. He lifted his toys with the truck and put them on his bed. Sam had a small car that could roll on the floor. He rolled his car on the rug and made vroom noises.

"Can I play with your truck, Tim?" Sam asked politely.

"No, you can't. It's mine and it's better than your car. You can only play with your car," Tim said rudely.

Sam felt sad, but he did not argue. He kept playing with his car. He saw a sock on the floor. He thought it would be fun to put the sock on his car and make it look like a hat. He picked up the sock and put it on his car.

"Hey, that's my sock!" Tim shouted. "Give it back to me!"

He grabbed the sock from Sam's car and pulled it hard. But the sock was stuck on the car. Tim pulled harder and harder, until the sock ripped in half. Tim was angry and threw the sock at Sam. Sam was hurt and cried.

"Look what you did, Tim! You broke my sock and hurt me!" Sam said.

"I don't care. It's your fault for taking my sock. You are a bad brother!" Tim said.

Tim and Sam stopped playing and did not talk to each other. They were both unhappy.

"Who did this?" she asked.

Tim nodded.

"Sam, did you take Tim's sock and put it on your car?" she asked.

Sam nodded.

"Why did you do that?" she asked.

Tim and Sam did not answer. They felt ashamed.

"You both did wrong. Tim, you should not be proud of your toys and refuse to share them with Sam. Sam, you should not take Tim's sock without asking. You should respect each other's things and feelings. You are brothers and you should love each other. Do you understand?" she said.

"I'm sorry, too," they said to each other.

Mom smiled and said she was glad they learned their lesson. She gave them each a kiss and a new sock. She told them to clean up their room and play nicely.

Tim and Sam did as they were told. They shared their toys and had fun. They were happy.

The end.

Foreshadowing or setup and payoff: The sock is introduced as a minor object on the floor, but later becomes the source of conflict and resolution. The truck and the car are contrasted as symbols of Tim's and Sam's personalities and values.

She took the mug and some colors and brushes and went to her room. She closed the door and started to paint. She painted a flower and a heart and a sun and wrote "I love you, Mom" on the mug. She was very proud of her work and smiled.

She put the mug on her desk and waited for it to dry. She wanted to wrap it and hide it until her mom's birthday. She heard a knock on the door. It was her brother, Ben.

"Can I come in?" he asked.

"No, go away!" Lily said. She did not want him to see the mug and spoil the surprise.

"Please, Lily, I need to talk to you," Ben said. He sounded sad and urgent.

Lily did not listen. She was angry and annoyed. She told him to leave her alone and not bother her. She did not care what he wanted to say.

Ben went away. He felt hurt and lonely. He had something important to tell Lily, but she did not care. He wished she was nicer to him and listened to him.

The next day, Lily woke up and saw the mug on her desk. It was dry and shiny and ready to be wrapped. She was very excited and happy. She took the mug and some paper and tape and went to the living room.

She saw Ben sitting on the couch. He looked sad and tired. He had a bandage on his arm and a bruise on his face. He had been in a fight at school and got hurt. He wanted to tell Lily about it, but she did not let him.

Lily felt sorry and guilty. She realized she had been mean and selfish. She had not cared about her brother's feelings and problems. She had only cared about her mug and her surprise.

She put the mug and the paper and the tape on the table. She went to Ben and hugged him. She said she was sorry and asked him what happened. She listened to him and comforted him. She told him she loved him and he was her best friend.

Ben smiled and hugged her back. He said he was sorry too and thanked her. He told her he loved her and she was his best sister.

Lily looked at the mug on the table. She had an idea. She asked Ben if he wanted to help her wrap it and give it to their mom as a surprise. She said it was a gift from both of them.

Ben agreed and smiled. He said it was a beautiful mug and their mom would love it. He said Lily was a gifted girl and a good sister.

They wrapped the mug together and hid it until their mom's birthday. They gave it to her and made her happy. They learned to be kind and caring to each other. They were a happy family.

"Let's bury some chocolate in the ground," Tom said. "Then we can dig it up later and have a surprise."

"OK," Lily said. "That sounds fun. But where should we bury it?"

"Let's bury it there," Tom said. "The dog won't find it, and neither will mom or dad."

"Where is the hole?" Lily asked. "I can't see it."

Tom looked around and saw a big mound of dirt. It was near the fence, under a tree.

"There it is," Tom said. "The dog must have dug it up again. Silly dog."

They ran to the mound and started to dig. They hoped their chocolate was still there. They dug and dug, but they did not find any chocolate. They only found bones and worms and rocks.

"Yuck," Lily said. "This is not chocolate. This is gross."

Tom was sad and angry. He threw the shovel on the ground.

"Bad dog," he said. "He ate our chocolate. He is a mean dog."

They heard a bark and saw their dog running towards them. He had chocolate on his mouth and paws. He wagged his tail and licked their faces.

"Stop it," Tom said. "Go away. You are a naughty dog."

But Lily laughed and hugged the dog. She did not mind the chocolate. She loved the dog.

"He is not a naughty dog," she said. "He is a silly dog. And we are silly too. We should not bury chocolate in the ground. We should eat it or share it."

Tom thought about it and nodded. He was not mad anymore. He loved the dog too.

"You are right," he said. "We are silly. And we still have some chocolate left. Let's go and eat it or share it."

They took the box of chocolate and went to the house. They gave some to their grandma and some to their mom and dad. They ate some themselves. They were happy and full.

The dog followed them and barked. He wanted some chocolate too.

But they knew chocolate was not good for dogs. They gave him a bone instead. He was happy and full too.

They all lived happily ever after. The end.

The water was cold and wet. Ben and Mia felt it on their feet and legs. They laughed and splashed each other. Sometimes a wave came and lifted them up. They liked that.

But one time, a wave was too strong and knocked Ben over. He fell into the water and got some in his mouth. He did not like that. He spit it out and made a face.

"Yuck, the water tastes salty!" he said, coughing.

"Are you okay, Ben?" dad asked, picking him up.

"I'm okay, dad, but the water is yucky," Ben said, wiping his mouth.

"It's okay, Ben, the water is supposed to be salty. It's from the ocean," dad said, hugging him.

"I don't like the ocean. I like the sand," Ben said, pointing to the beach.

"Okay, let's go back to the sand then. We can make a sandcastle," dad said, carrying him to the shore.

"Yay, a sandcastle!" Ben said, feeling better.

Mia followed them with mom. She liked the water and the sand. She liked the beach. She was very enthusiastic.

"Wow, can we use it too? Can we go to faraway lands and see new things?" Lily asked.

"Maybe we can. Let's pack our bags and go to the airport. We can find a plane that will take us somewhere fun," Tom said.

They took their backpacks and stuffed them with some clothes, snacks, and toys. They also took the passport and some money they found in their mom's purse. They sneaked out of the house and walked to the bus stop. They saw a bus that said "Airport" on it, and they got on.

At the airport, they saw many people and planes. They looked for a sign that said where the planes were going. They saw one that said "Paris". They remembered that Paris was a beautiful city in France, where they spoke a different language.

"Let's go to Paris, Lily. It sounds like a fun place. Maybe we can see the Eiffel Tower and eat some cheese," Tom said.

"OK, Tom. But how do we get on the plane? We need a ticket, right?" Lily said.

"Don't worry, Lily. We have dad's passport. That's like a ticket. We just have to show it to the people at the gate, and they will let us on," Tom said.

They found the gate that said "Paris" and waited in line. When it was their turn, they gave the passport to the lady at the desk. She looked at it and then at them. She frowned and said something in a language they didn't understand. She called another lady, who came and looked at them too. They both looked angry and scared.

"Who are you? Where are your parents? This is not your passport. This is a very serious matter. You can't just take someone else's passport and try to board a plane. You are in big trouble. We have to call the police and your parents right away," the second lady said in English.

Tom and Lily didn't understand what was happening. They felt scared and sorry. They wished they had never taken the passport. They wished they had stayed at home and played with their toys. They started to cry and hug each other. They knew they had done something very bad, and they would be punished. They missed their dad and mom, and they hoped they would forgive them.

"Can I help you, mom?" Lily asked.

"Sure, honey. You can serve the cake to dad when it is ready. But first, we have to wait for the cake to bake in the oven. It will take twenty minutes," her mom said.

Lily nodded. She was excited to serve the cake to dad. She thought he would be very happy and proud of her. She looked at the clock on the wall. It had two big hands and many small numbers. She did not know what they meant, but her mom did.

"Mom, how do you know when twenty minutes are over?" Lily asked.

"Well, you see the big hand on the clock? It moves around the clock very slowly. When it moves from one number to another, that is one minute. When it moves around the whole clock, that is one hour. Twenty minutes are when the big hand moves from one number to ten numbers ahead," her mom explained.

Lily tried to follow her mom's words, but she was confused. She did not understand how the big hand could move so slowly and still tell the time. She decided to watch the clock and count the numbers.

One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten. Lily counted in her head. She saw the big hand move from one number to ten numbers ahead. She thought that was twenty minutes. She jumped up and ran to the oven.

"Mom, mom, the cake is ready! I can serve it to dad now!" she shouted.

She opened the oven door and reached for the cake. But the cake was very hot and burned her hand. She screamed and dropped the cake. It fell on the floor and broke into pieces.

"Oh, Lily, what have you done?" her mom said. She ran to Lily and hugged her. She checked her hand and saw a red mark. She put some ice on it and kissed it.

"I'm sorry, mom. I wanted to serve the cake to dad. I thought it was twenty minutes. I counted the numbers on the clock," Lily said.

"Lily, you counted wrong. You counted ten minutes, not twenty. You have to wait for the big hand to move around the clock twice, not once. That is twenty minutes. You were too impatient and did not listen to me. You have to be careful with the oven. It is very hot and dangerous. You could have hurt yourself badly," her mom said.

Lily felt bad. She did not mean to ruin the cake and hurt herself. She did not want to make her mom and dad sad. She learned a lesson. She learned to be patient and listen to her mom. She learned to not touch the oven without her mom's help. She learned to check the time with her mom before doing something.

They had fun playing for a while, until Ben saw something shiny in the water. He reached for it, but his boat tipped over and his ball fell out. He tried to grab it, but it rolled away and went down the drain.

"Uh-oh," Ben said, looking at the empty hole. "My apples are gone!"

Mia saw what happened and sailed over to Ben. She saw his sad face and felt sorry for him.

"I'm sorry, Ben," she said, giving him a hug. "That was a nice ball. Do you want to share my flower?"

Ben smiled and nodded. He took the flower and put it in his boat. He thanked Mia for being a good friend.

They sailed back to the harbor and put their boats away. They decided to play something else, but they never forgot their adventure in the tub.

"Why did you touch my dog?" he asked Lily. "You should know better. My dog is not friendly. He does not like strangers. You are lucky he did not hurt you more."

Lily was sorry. She did not mean to make the dog angry. She was just curious. She liked animals. She wanted to be friends with the dog.

"I'm sorry, mister," she said. "I just wanted to pet your dog. He looked nice. I did not know he was not friendly."

The man shook his head. He took his dog and left. He did not say anything more.

Lily was afraid. She did not like shots. She wished she had listened to Tom. She wished she had not touched the dog. She wished she had not been ignorant.

She learned a hard lesson. She learned to remember to ask before touching. She learned to respect animals. She learned to be careful. She learned that ignorance can have a bad result.

"Stop, Lily, stop!" Ben shouted. "You are hurting the poppies. They need to stay in the ground. They are not for us to use."

But Lily did not stop. She picked and picked and picked. She made a big pile of poppies. She tried to make a poppy crown, but the poppies were too soft and wilted. They fell apart in her hands.

"Look, Lily, look what you did," Ben said. "You wasted the poppies. They are not pretty anymore. They are sad and brown. And the bees and birds and bugs have no food. You were selfish and greedy."

Lily looked at the poppies. She felt bad. She saw the bees and birds and bugs flying away. She saw the empty field. She saw Ben's angry face.

"Sure, you can come with me," Lily said. "But you have to be quiet. Mommy doesn't like it when I talk to my drawings."

Lily folded Anna and put her in her pocket. She went to the kitchen and saw that Mommy had made sandwiches and soup for lunch. She sat down at the table and took Anna out of her pocket. She put her on the napkin next to her plate.

"Here, Anna, you can have some of my sandwich," Lily whispered. She tore a small piece of bread and cheese and gave it to Anna.

"Thank you, Lily," Anna whispered back. She took the bread and cheese and put it in her mouth.

But as soon as she did, something strange happened. Anna's head began to grow bigger and bigger. It filled the whole napkin and then the whole table. Lily was scared. She dropped her spoon and screamed.

"Mommy, Mommy, help! Anna's head is too big!"

Mommy heard Lily's scream and ran to the kitchen. She saw Lily's drawing on the table, with a huge head and a small body. She was shocked.

"Lily, what did you do?" Mommy asked.

"I don't know, Mommy," Lily cried. "I just gave her some of my sandwich. I wanted to share with her. She was my friend."

Mommy looked at the drawing and saw that it had a mouth, a nose, eyes and hair. She realized that Lily had created a magic friend with her crayons. She remembered that she had given Lily a special set of crayons for her birthday. They were magic crayons that could make anything come to life.

Mommy hugged Lily and calmed her down. She told her that she was not angry with her, but that she had to be careful with her crayons. She explained that some things were not meant to be eaten, like paper and crayons. She said that Anna was not a real friend, but a drawing that Lily had created with her imagination.

She took the drawing and the crayons and put them in a safe place. She told Lily that she could play with them again, but only under her supervision. She said that Lily had a wonderful gift of creativity, but that she had to use it wisely.

She made Lily a new sandwich and soup and ate with her. She told her that she loved her very much and that she was proud of her. She said that Lily had many real friends who cared for her and wanted to play with her.

Lily felt better. She ate her lunch and thanked Mommy. She said that she loved Mommy very much and that she was sorry for making a mess. She said that she still liked Anna, but that she understood that she was not a real friend. She said that she wanted to play with her real friends later.

Mommy smiled and kissed Lily. She said that she was glad that Lily learned her lesson. She said that she would always be there for her and help her with her creativity. She said that Lily was a very special and smart girl. She said that she was her best friend.

But his mom said, "Sam, it is time for bed. You have to stop doing math and brush your teeth."

Sam did not want to stop. He said, "No, mom, I want to do more math. Math is fun. I can do one more problem, please."

His mom said, "Sam, you are being stubborn. You have done enough math for today. You need to sleep and rest your brain. You can do more math tomorrow."

Sam did not listen. He hid his math book under his pillow. He said, "Okay, mom, I will go to bed. But I will do more math when you are not looking."

His mom said, "Sam, I know what you are doing. You cannot trick me. I will not let you do more math. You have to give me your math book now."

Sam did not want to give his math book. He held it tight. He said, "No, mom, it is my math book. You cannot have it. I love math. Math is mine."

His mom said, "Sam, you are being very naughty. You have to share your math book. Math is not only yours. Math is for everyone. You can love math, but you have to follow the rules. The rule is, no math after bedtime."

Sam did not like the rule. He said, "That is a bad rule. I do not like that rule. I want to make my own rule. My rule is, math anytime I want."

His mom said, "Sam, you cannot make your own rule. You have to respect the rule. The rule is for your own good. Math is good, but too much math is not good. You have to balance math with other things. Like sleep, and play, and eat, and read, and hug."

Sam thought about it. He liked sleep, and play, and eat, and read, and hug. He said, "Okay, mom, maybe you are right. Maybe too much math is not good. Maybe I need to balance math with other things. But can I do one more problem, please?"

Lila said, "I do."

Lila's mom said, "Do you, Ben, take Lila to be your wife?"

One day, they saw something new in the water. It was big and round and clear, with long thin things hanging from it. It looked like a balloon with strings. Anna and Ben were curious. They wanted to touch it.

"Look, Mom, look, Dad, what is that?" they asked.

Mom and Dad looked at the water and saw the thing. They knew what it was. It was a jellyfish.

"Be careful, Anna, be careful, Ben, that is a jellyfish. It can hurt you if you touch it. It can sting you with its long thin things. Stay away from it," they said.

Anna and Ben were scared. They did not want to touch the jellyfish. They did not want to get hurt. They ran away from the water and back to the sand.

But there was another child at the beach. He was shy and did not have any friends. He saw the jellyfish too. He was not scared. He was brave. He wanted to have a friend. He thought the jellyfish looked lonely.

He went to the water and picked up the jellyfish. He did not feel any sting. He felt only soft and wet. He smiled. He carried the jellyfish to his towel. He put it down gently. He talked to it. He said, "Hello, jellyfish, I am Sam. Do you want to be my friend?"

The jellyfish did not say anything. It did not move. It did not look happy. It looked sad. It missed the water. It needed the water to live.

Sam did not know that. He thought the jellyfish was shy like him. He wanted to make it happy. He said, "Don't be shy, jellyfish, I am nice. I will take care of you. I will share my toys with you. Do you want to play with me?"

Sam did not understand. He thought the jellyfish was rude. He felt sad. He said, "Why don't you talk to me, jellyfish? Why don't you like me? Are you not my friend?"

The jellyfish did not reply. It did not like Sam. It did not want to be his friend. It wanted to be alone.

"Are you sure this is a good idea?" Sam asked Ben. He was a little scared of the dark and the noises.

"Don't be a baby," Ben said. "It will be fun. I want to see what's in the woods. Maybe we'll find some animals or treasure."

They walked for a long time, but they did not see anything interesting. The woods were icy and cold. The flashlight was not very bright. Sam started to shiver and wished they were back home.

"Ben, I think we should go back," Sam said. "It's too late and too cold. And I don't like this place. It's creepy."

"Fine, fine," Ben said. "But you're such a chicken. You never want to try anything new. I recommend you be more brave and adventurous."

They turned around and tried to find their way back. But they soon realized they were lost. They had walked too far and did not remember where they came from. They started to panic and cry.

"Help! Help!" they shouted. But no one heard them. The woods were too big and too quiet.

They hugged each other and hoped someone would find them. But no one did. They froze to death in the icy woods.

The moral of the story is: Do not go out at night without telling your parents. And do not be too proud or stubborn to listen to your friends. Sometimes, it is better to be safe than sorry.

"They do feel, Ben. They are alive. They need water and sun and soil. If you pick them, they will die. And then there will be no more flowers in the park," Anna said, trying to explain.

Ben looked at the flower in his hand. He saw that it was wilting and losing its color. He felt sorry for the flower. He remembered that his mom had told him the same thing once, when he had picked a flower from her garden.

"You are right, Anna. I am sorry. I will not pick any more flowers. I will put this one back in the ground. Maybe it will grow again," Ben said, putting the flower back where he had found it.

"Thank you, Ben. That is very kind of you. Maybe the flower will be happy again. And maybe the bees and the birds and the bugs will be happy too," Anna said, smiling.

They hugged and continued to play in the park, looking at the wild flowers and enjoying their beauty.

One day, a little boy named Sam went to the zoo with his mom and dad. He liked to see all the different animals, but his favorite was the leopard. He wanted to see how fast and strong the leopard was.

He saw a big cage with a sign that said "Leopard". He ran to the cage and looked inside. He saw a big, yellow cat with black spots. The cat was lying on a rock and licking its paw. Sam thought the cat was very pretty, but also very lazy.

"Hello, leopard!" Sam said. "Do you want to play with me?"

The leopard heard Sam and looked at him. It saw a small, brown boy with curly hair. The boy was smiling and waving. The leopard thought the boy was very noisy, but also very curious.

"Hello, boy," the leopard said. "What do you want to play?"

Sam thought for a moment. He liked to play many games, but he wanted to play something that the leopard would like too.

"How about we play roll?" Sam said. "You roll on the ground and I roll on the grass. We can see who can roll faster and farther."

The leopard thought for a moment. It liked to roll on the ground sometimes, but it was not very interested in rolling on the grass. It was more interested in sleeping on the rock.

"Sorry, boy," the leopard said. "I don't want to play roll. I want to rest on my rock. Maybe you can find another animal to play with."

Sam felt sad. He really wanted to play with the leopard, but the leopard did not want to play with him. He looked around and saw other animals in other cages. He saw a monkey, a giraffe, a lion, and a penguin. He wondered if any of them would want to play roll with him.

He decided to try the monkey first. He ran to the cage with the sign that said "Monkey". He saw a small, brown animal with a long tail. The animal was swinging from a branch and making funny noises. Sam thought the animal was very silly, but also very fun.

"Hello, monkey!" Sam said. "Do you want to play roll with me?"

The monkey heard Sam and looked at him. It saw a small, brown boy with curly hair. The boy was smiling and waving. The monkey thought the boy was very friendly, but also very strange.

"Hello, boy," the monkey said. "What is roll?"

Sam explained the game to the monkey. He showed him how to roll on the grass and how to have fun.

The monkey liked the game. It jumped from the branch and rolled on the ground. It laughed and clapped its hands.

"Roll is fun!" the monkey said. "I want to play roll with you!"

Sam was happy. He found a friend who wanted to play with him. He rolled on the grass and laughed with the monkey. They had a lot of fun.

The leopard watched them from its cage. It saw the boy and the monkey rolling and laughing. It felt a little jealous. It wondered if it was missing something.

Maybe roll was not so bad. Maybe it could try it too.

The leopard got up from its rock and walked to the edge of its cage. It looked at the boy and the monkey and said:

"Hey, boy. Hey, monkey. Can I play roll with you too?"

Sam and the monkey heard the leopard and looked at it. They saw a big, yellow cat with black spots. The cat was standing and smiling. Sam and the monkey thought the cat was very pretty, but also very brave.

"Sure, leopard," Sam said. "You can play roll with us. We have room for one more."

The leopard was happy. It thanked the boy and the monkey and joined them. It rolled on the ground and laughed with them. It had a lot of fun.

The three of them played roll for a long time. They became good friends. They learned that they had more in common than they thought.

They learned that roll was a game for everyone.

"Let's go and see!" Ben said. He was brave and curious.

"No, we can't!" Lily said. She was careful and scared. "It's not our house. Mommy said we can't go into other people's houses."

"Maybe there is a fire in there!" he thought. He wanted to make a fire. He liked fire. It was warm and light. He took a match from his pocket and lit it. He threw it into the chimney.

"I'm sorry, mister. I didn't mean to make a fire. I was curious. Please don't be mad at me."

The man looked at Ben. He saw that he was a little boy who made a mistake. He was still angry, but he was also kind.

"It's okay, kid. I forgive you. But don't ever do that again. Fire is dangerous. It can hurt you and others. You have to be careful and listen to your sister. She is smart and knows what's right."

"Can we eat them now?" asks Ben.

"Yes, we can eat them now. But we have to wash them first," says Anna.

"Mmm, these are the best blueberries ever," says Ben.

"I agree. They are yummy," says Anna.

One day, a big lion and a small mouse met in the forest. The lion was hungry and wanted to eat the mouse. The mouse was scared and begged the lion to let him go.

"Please, Mr. Lion, do not eat me. I am too small and not tasty. If you let me go, I will be your friend and help you someday." The mouse said.

The lion laughed and said, "How can you help me? You are so weak and tiny. I am the king of the forest. No one can help me. But I am jolly today, so I will let you go. But do not forget, you owe me a favor."

The mouse thanked the lion and ran away. He was happy and relieved.

Some time later, the lion was caught in a big net by some hunters. He roared and struggled, but he could not break free. He felt angry and sad. He thought he would die.

The mouse heard the lion's roar and came to see what was wrong. He saw the lion trapped in the net and felt sorry for him. He remembered the lion's kindness and decided to help him.

He ran to the net and started to bite the ropes with his sharp teeth. He worked hard and fast, and soon he made a hole in the net. He told the lion to crawl out and run away.

The lion was amazed and grateful. He said, "Thank you, little mouse. You have saved my life. You are a true friend. I was wrong to think you could not help me. You are brave and smart. I am sorry for being proud and mean. From now on, I will be kind and humble to everyone."

The mouse smiled and said, "You are welcome, Mr. Lion. I am glad you are safe. You have learned a good lesson. Never judge someone by their size or appearance. Everyone has something to offer. And never forget to repay a favor. That is what friends do."

The lion and the mouse hugged and became friends. They lived happily in the forest and helped each other. They also taught other animals to be respectful and generous. They showed that friendship is stronger than fear and pride.

Some people like it, some people don't, but you have to try it before you decide. Maybe you will like it, maybe you won't, but you will never know if you don't try. Please, eat your sandwich and drink your water, and then you can go outside and play with your ball. Okay?"

Tommy looked at his mom and saw that she was not mean and unfair, but kind and caring. He felt sorry for making her sad and for being rude and stubborn. He nodded and said, "Okay, mom. I will try the sandwich. But can you cut off the crusts? I don't like the crusts."

His mom smiled and said, "Sure, I can cut off the crusts. But you have to promise me to eat the rest of the sandwich, and to try new things when I give them to you. Deal?"

Tommy said, "Deal." He ate his sandwich and drank his water. He found that the pepper was not too hot, but a little spicy and interesting. He liked the cheese and the bread, too. He felt full and satisfied. He thanked his mom and gave her a kiss. He said, "I love you, mom. You are the best."

His mom said, "I love you, too, Tommy. You are a good boy. Now you can go outside and play with your ball. Have fun, but be careful."

Tommy went outside and played with his ball. He had fun, but he also learned a lesson. He learned that his mom loved him and wanted him to be well. He learned that eating his food was important and good for him. He learned that trying new things was not scary, but exciting. He learned that pepper was not bad, but different. He learned that being restless was not always good, but sometimes he had to be calm and listen. He learned that being a good boy made him and his mom happy. He learned that he loved his mom and his sandwich, even with pepper on it.
